```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any


class SQLError(Exception):
    """Base class for all minisql errors."""
    pass


class SQLSyntaxError(SQLError):
    """Raised when tokenize or parse encounters invalid syntax."""
    
    def __init__(self, message: str, pos: int):
        self.pos = pos
        super().__init__(f"{message} at position {pos}")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Token:
    kind: str
    value: Any
    pos: int


KEYWORDS = {
    "SELECT", "FROM", "WHERE", "AND", "OR", "NOT", 
    "ORDER", "BY", "ASC", "DESC", "LIMIT", 
    "IS", "NULL", "TRUE", "FALSE",
    "JOIN", "ON", "GROUP", "AS", "COUNT", "SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX"
}


def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
    """
    Tokenize a SQL string into a list of Tokens, ending with an EOF token.
    """
    tokens: list[Token] = []
    i = 0
    n = len(sql)

    while i < n:
        # Skip whitespace
        if sql[i].isspace():
            i += 1
            continue

        start = i
        char = sql[i]

        # Identifiers and Keywords
        if char.isalpha() or char == '_':
            while i < n and (sql[i].isalnum() or sql[i] == '_'):
                i += 1
            word = sql[start:i]
            upper_word = word.upper()
            if upper_word in KEYWORDS:
                tokens.append(Token("KEYWORD", upper_word, start))
            else:
                tokens.append(Token("IDENT", word, start))
            continue

        # Numbers
        if char.isdigit() or (char == '-' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1].isdigit()):
            # Check for negative sign
            if char == '-':
                i += 1  # consume '-'
            
            # Consume digits
            while i < n and sql[i].isdigit():
                i += 1
            
            is_float = False
            # Check for fractional part
            if i < n and sql[i] == '.':
                # Must have digits after dot
                if i + 1 >= n or not sql[i+1].isdigit():
                    raise SQLSyntaxError("Invalid number format", i)
                is_float = True
                i += 1  # consume '.'
                while i < n and sql[i].isdigit():
                    i += 1
            
            num_str = sql[start:i]
            if is_float:
                val = float(num_str)
            else:
                val = int(num_str)
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", val, start))
            continue

        # Strings
        if char == "'":
            j = i + 1
            val_chars = []
            terminated = False
            while j < n:
                if sql[j] == "'":
                    if j + 1 < n and sql[j+1] == "'":
                        val_chars.append("'")
                        j += 2
                    else:
                        terminated = True
                        break
                else:
                    val_chars.append(sql[j])
                    j += 1
            
            if not terminated:
                raise SQLSyntaxError("Unterminated string literal", start)
            
            val = "".join(val_chars)
            i = j + 1 # move past closing quote
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", val, start))
            continue

        # Operators
        if char == '!' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1] == '=':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '!=', start))
            i += 2
            continue
        if char == '<' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1] == '>':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '!=', start))
            i += 2
            continue
        if char == '<' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1] == '=':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '<=', start))
            i += 2
            continue
        if char == '>' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1] == '=':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '>=', start))
            i += 2
            continue
        if char == '<':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '<', start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == '>':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '>', start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == '=':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '=', start))
            i += 1
            continue

        # Punctuation
        if char == '*':
            tokens.append(Token("STAR", "*", start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == ',':
            tokens.append(Token("COMMA", ",", start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == '(':
            tokens.append(Token("LPAREN", "(", start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == ')':
            tokens.append(Token("RPAREN", ")", start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == '.':
            tokens.append(Token("DOT", ".", start))
            i += 1
            continue

        # Unknown character
        raise SQLSyntaxError(f"Unexpected character '{char}'", start)

    tokens.append(Token("EOF", None, len(sql)))
    return tokens
```

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any


class SQLError(Exception):
    """Base class for all minisql errors."""
    pass


class SQLSyntaxError(SQLError):
    """Raised when tokenize or parse encounters invalid syntax."""
    
    def __init__(self, message: str, pos: int):
        self.pos = pos
        super().__init__(f"{message} at position {pos}")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Token:
    kind: str
    value: Any
    pos: int


KEYWORDS = {
    "SELECT", "FROM", "WHERE", "AND", "OR", "NOT", 
    "ORDER", "BY", "ASC", "DESC", "LIMIT", 
    "IS", "NULL", "TRUE", "FALSE",
    "JOIN", "ON", "GROUP", "AS", "COUNT", "SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX"
}


def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
    """
    Tokenize a SQL string into a list of Tokens, ending with an EOF token.
    """
    tokens: list[Token] = []
    i = 0
    n = len(sql)

    while i < n:
        # Skip whitespace
        if sql[i].isspace():
            i += 1
            continue

        start = i
        char = sql[i]

        # Identifiers and Keywords
        if char.isalpha() or char == '_':
            while i < n and (sql[i].isalnum() or sql[i] == '_'):
                i += 1
            word = sql[start:i]
            upper_word = word.upper()
            if upper_word in KEYWORDS:
                tokens.append(Token("KEYWORD", upper_word, start))
            else:
                tokens.append(Token("IDENT", word, start))
            continue

        # Numbers
        if char.isdigit() or (char == '-' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1].isdigit()):
            # Check for negative sign
            if char == '-':
                i += 1  # consume '-'
            
            # Consume digits
            while i < n and sql[i].isdigit():
                i += 1
            
            is_float = False
            # Check for fractional part
            if i < n and sql[i] == '.':
                # Must have digits after dot
                if i + 1 >= n or not sql[i+1].isdigit():
                    raise SQLSyntaxError("Invalid number format", i)
                is_float = True
                i += 1  # consume '.'
                while i < n and sql[i].isdigit():
                    i += 1
            
            num_str = sql[start:i]
            if is_float:
                val = float(num_str)
            else:
                val = int(num_str)
            tokens.append(Token("NUMBER", val, start))
            continue

        # Strings
        if char == "'":
            j = i + 1
            val_chars = []
            terminated = False
            while j < n:
                if sql[j] == "'":
                    if j + 1 < n and sql[j+1] == "'":
                        val_chars.append("'")
                        j += 2
                    else:
                        terminated = True
                        break
                else:
                    val_chars.append(sql[j])
                    j += 1
            
            if not terminated:
                raise SQLSyntaxError("Unterminated string literal", start)
            
            val = "".join(val_chars)
            i = j + 1 # move past closing quote
            tokens.append(Token("STRING", val, start))
            continue

        # Operators
        if char == '!' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1] == '=':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '!=', start))
            i += 2
            continue
        if char == '<' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1] == '>':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '!=', start))
            i += 2
            continue
        if char == '<' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1] == '=':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '<=', start))
            i += 2
            continue
        if char == '>' and i + 1 < n and sql[i+1] == '=':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '>=', start))
            i += 2
            continue
        if char == '<':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '<', start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == '>':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '>', start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == '=':
            tokens.append(Token("OP", '=', start))
            i += 1
            continue

        # Punctuation
        if char == '*':
            tokens.append(Token("STAR", "*", start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == ',':
            tokens.append(Token("COMMA", ",", start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == '(':
            tokens.append(Token("LPAREN", "(", start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == ')':
            tokens.append(Token("RPAREN", ")", start))
            i += 1
            continue
        if char == '.':
            tokens.append(Token("DOT", ".", start))
            i += 1
            continue

        # Unknown character
        raise SQLSyntaxError(f"Unexpected character '{char}'", start)

    tokens.append(Token("EOF", None, len(sql)))
    return tokens
```

        token = self.tokens[self.pos]

        if expected_value is not None and token.value != expected_value:

        self.pos += 1

            self.consume()
            parts.append(".")

            blocks.append(block)
            continue

            blocks.append(('heading', level, heading_text))
            continue
        
        # Rule 3: Horizontal rule
        if _is_hr(line):
            blocks.append(('hr',))
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # Rule 4: Blockquote
        if line.startswith('>'):
            block, i = _parse_blockquote(lines, i)
            blocks.append(block)
            continue
        
        # Rule 5: List

            block, i = _parse_list(lines, i)
            blocks.append(block)
            continue
        
        # Rule 6: Table
        if _is_table_start(lines, i):
            block, i = _parse_table(lines, i)
            blocks.append(block)
            continue
        
        # Rule 7: Paragraph
        text_lines, i = _parse_paragraph(lines, i)
        blocks.append(('paragraph', text_lines))
    
    return blocks

    # Must start at beginning of line (no leading spaces)

    # Remove trailing # if it's the whole text or preceded by whitespace
    if raw_text == '#' * len(raw_text) and len(raw_text) > 0:

    else:

            raw_text = raw_text.rstrip('#')

        line = lines[i]

            if _is_table_start(lines, i):

        i += 1
    
    return ('\n'.join(para_lines), i)

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Optional

class MachineError(Exception):
    """Base exception for the FSM library."""
    pass

class InvalidTransition(MachineError):
    """Raised when no transition exists for the event from the current state."""
    def __init__(self, state: str, event: str):
        super().__init__(f"No transition for event '{event}' from state '{state}'")
        self.state = state
        self.event = event

class GuardRejected(MachineError):
    """Raised when all transitions for the event are rejected by guards."""
    def __init__(self, state: str, event: str):
        super().__init__(f"Guard rejected for event '{event}' from state '{state}'")
        self.state = state
        self.event = event

@dataclass
class State:
    name: str
    on_enter: Optional[callable] = None
    on_exit: Optional[callable] = None

@dataclass
class Transition:
    event: str
    source: Any  # str, list[str], tuple[str, ...], or '*'
    target: Optional[str]
    guard: Optional[callable] = None
    action: Optional[callable] = None

@dataclass
class Event:
    name: str
    source: str
    target: str
    data: dict

class Machine:
    def __init__(self, states: list, transitions: list[Transition], initial: str, context: Any = None):
        if not states:
            raise ValueError("states list is empty")
        
        self._states = {}
        for s in states:
            if isinstance(s, str):
                state_obj = State(name=s)
            else:
                state_obj = s
            
            if state_obj.name in self._states:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate state name: {state_obj.name}")
            self._states[state_obj.name] = state_obj
        
        if initial not in self._states:
            raise ValueError(f"Initial state '{initial}' is not defined")
        
        self._initial = initial
        self.state = initial
        self.context = context
        self.history: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
        
        self._transitions: list[Transition] = []
        for t in transitions:
            # Validate source
            if t.source == '*':
                pass
            elif isinstance(t.source, (list, tuple)):
                for src in t.source:
                    if src not in self._states:
                        raise ValueError(f"Transition source '{src}' is not a state")
            elif isinstance(t.source, str):
                if t.source not in self._states:
                    raise ValueError(f"Transition source '{t.source}' is not a state")
            
            # Validate target
            if t.target is not None and t.target not in self._states:
                raise ValueError(f"Transition target '{t.target}' is not a state")
            
            self._transitions.append(t)
        
        self._listeners: list[callable] = []
        self._fire_depth = 0

    def _matches_source(self, trans: Transition, current_state: str) -> bool:
        if trans.source == '*':
            return True
        if isinstance(trans.source, str):
            return trans.source == current_state
        if isinstance(trans.source, (list, tuple)):
            return current_state in trans.source
        return False

    def fire(self, event_name: str, **data: Any) -> str:
        if self._fire_depth > 0:
            raise MachineError("Cannot call fire recursively")
        
        self._fire_depth += 1
        try:
            # Find candidates
            candidates = [
                t for t in self._transitions
                if t.event == event_name and self._matches_source(t, self.state)
            ]
            
            if not candidates:
                raise InvalidTransition(self.state, event_name)
            
            # Create shared data dict for all Events in this call
            shared_data = dict(data)
            
            # Find first candidate that passes guard
            selected_transition = None
            for t in candidates:
                # Determine target for guard evaluation
                # For guard, target is the current state (or target if normal)
                # But spec says: target is state transition leads to (for internal, current state)
                # Let's resolve target now
                if t.target is None:
                    resolved_target = self.state
                else:
                    resolved_target = t.target
                
                ev = Event(
                    name=event_name,
                    source=self.state,
                    target=resolved_target,
                    data=shared_data
                )
                
                if t.guard is None or t.guard(self, ev):
                    selected_transition = t
                    break
            
            if selected_transition is None:
                raise GuardRejected(self.state, event_name)
            
            t = selected_transition
            current_state_name = self.state
            
            # Resolve target
            if t.target is None:
                new_state_name = current_state_name
                is_internal = True
            else:
                new_state_name = t.target
                is_internal = False
            
            # Build the event object for hooks
            # source is current state, target is the resolved target
            ev = Event(
                name=event_name,
                source=current_state_name,
                target=new_state_name,
                data=shared_data
            )
            
            if is_internal:
                # Internal transition
                # 1. Run action
                if t.action:
                    t.action(self, ev)
                
                # 2. Record history
                self.history.append((current_state_name, event_name, current_state_name))
                
                # 3. Call listeners
                for listener in self._listeners:
                    listener(current_state_name, ev, current_state_name)
                
                # Return current state
                return current_state_name
            else:
                # Normal transition
                # 1. Run on_exit of current state
                source_state = self._states[current_state_name]
                if source_state.on_exit:
                    source_state.on_exit(self, ev)
                
                # 2. Run transition action
                if t.action:
                    t.action(self, ev)
                
                # 3. Set new state and record history
                self.state = new_state_name
                self.history.append((current_state_name, event_name, new_state_name))
                
                # 4. Run on_enter of new state
                target_state = self._states[new_state_name]
                if target_state.on_enter:
                    target_state.on_enter(self, ev)
                
                # 5. Call listeners
                for listener in self._listeners:
                    listener(current_state_name, ev, new_state_name)
                
                return new_state_name
                
        finally:
            self._fire_depth -= 1

    def can_fire(self, event_name: str, **data: Any) -> bool:
        # Find candidates
        candidates = [
            t for t in self._transitions
            if t.event == event_name and self._matches_source(t, self.state)
        ]
        
        if not candidates:
            return False
        
        shared_data = dict(data)
        
        for t in candidates:
            if t.target is None:
                resolved_target = self.state
            else:
                resolved_target = t.target
            
            ev = Event(
                name=event_name,
                source=self.state,
                target=resolved_target,
                data=shared_data
            )
            
            if t.guard is None or t.guard(self, ev):
                return True
        
        return False

    def available_events(self) -> list[str]:
        events = set()
        for t in self._transitions:
            if self._matches_source(t, self.state):
                events.add(t.event)
        return sorted(events)

    def on_transition(self, listener: callable) -> None:
        self._listeners.append(listener)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.state = self._initial
        self.history = []
```

rounds.critique:
### 1. Broken State Consistency in `vending.py` (`select` and `cancel` methods)
The specification explicitly states: **"its attribute `machine` is the `fsm.Machine` it uses, and `machine.state` is always equal to the vending machine's `state`."**

In `vending.py`, both `select()` and `cancel()` mutate the internal credit **before** the state transition occurs:
- In `select`, `select_action` calculates change and sets `machine.context['credit'] = 0` **before** `fire` proceeds to set `machine.state` to `'idle'`.
- In `cancel`, `cancel_action` sets `machine.context['credit'] = 0` **before** `fire` proceeds to set `machine.state` to `'idle'`.

Because the credit is mutated during the action (or effectively before the state change logic in the wrapper completes), there is a window where the logical state of the Vending Machine (determined by credit > 0) contradicts the FSM state.
1. **Consistency Violation:** While `fire` is executing the action, `machine.state` is still `'credit'`, but the logical "Vending Machine State" (based on credit) has effectively changed to 'idle' logic (credit 0). If a listener or hook checks consistency here, it fails.
2. **Race Condition/Logic Error:** More critically, `select` and `cancel` return the change by popping from `context['_last_change']`. If `fire` raises an exception *after* the action but *before* the state update (e.g., an `on_enter` hook on the target state fails), the specification says: *"If it comes from ... the action, the state and history are unchanged."* However, the action has already modified `context['credit']` to 0. The Vending Machine object is now corrupted: `credit` is 0, but `state` is `'credit'`. A subsequent `cancel()` would return 0 refund despite the machine being in `'credit'`.

**Fix Required:** The state change (credit reset) should be coupled strictly with the state transition completion, or the `select/cancel` methods should only apply the credit reset *after* `fire` successfully returns. Currently, the mutation happens inside the FSM action, which violates the atomicity implied by the consistency requirement when exceptions occur during hooks.

### 2. Incorrect Handling of Insert Transition Semantics in `vending.py`
The specification says: **"`insert(coin: int) -> int` | `idle`, `credit` | Adds the coin to the credit, moves to `credit`, returns the new credit."**

The implementation defines two separate transitions:
1. `idle` -> `credit`
2. `credit` -> `credit`

While this technically works for state names, the spec implies a unified behavior. More importantly, the **guard/check for invalid coins** is implemented inside the `action`.
- Spec: *"A coin that is not accepted raises `ValueError` and changes nothing."*
- Spec on FSM: *"An exception raised by any hook propagates unchanged out of `fire`. If it comes from a guard, `on_exit` or the action, the state and `history` are unchanged."*

In the code, `insert_action` raises `ValueError` if the coin is invalid. Since it is an `action`, `fire` will propagate the error and *not* change the state or history. This meets the "changes nothing" requirement for the FSM state/history. However, `insert_action` also modifies `machine.context['credit']` **before** raising the error in some logic flows?
Let's look closely at `insert_action`:
```python
def insert_action(machine: Machine, event: fsm.Event):
    coin = event.data['coin']
    if coin not in VendingMachine.COINS:
        raise ValueError(f"Coin {coin} not accepted")
    machine.context['credit'] += coin # This runs ONLY if valid
```
This logic is actually correct regarding the "changes nothing" rule for invalid coins.

**However**, there is a subtle issue with `select` and `cancel` described in point 1. The issue is that `select_action` modifies `context['credit']` to 0. If `select_action` succeeds, but then the state transition fails (e.g., a hypothetical `on_enter` hook on 'idle' fails), the credit is gone, but the machine is still in 'credit'. This breaks the "unchanged" requirement for the *Vending Machine's logical state* even if the FSM state is unchanged. The spec says "A failed `select` leaves the credit... unchanged." Since the credit is in `context`, and `context` is not rolled back by `Machine`, modifying `context` inside `action` is unsafe if any subsequent step in `fire` can fail.

### 3. `available_events` does not respect the "ignoring guards" requirement correctly in edge cases?
Spec: **"`available_events() -> list[str]`: the sorted, de-duplicated names of the events that have at least one transition from the current state, ignoring guards."**
The implementation:
```python
def available_events(self) -> list[str]:
    events = set()
    for t in self._transitions:
        if self._matches_source(t, self.state):
            events.add(t.event)
    return sorted(events)
```
This correctly ignores guards. It checks if a transition *exists* from the state. This part is correct.

### 4. `Machine.fire` recursion check
Spec: **"Calling `fire` on a machine while one of its `fire` calls is still running (from inside a hook) raises `MachineError`."**
The implementation uses `self._fire_depth`. This is correct.

### 5. `fsm/machine.py` `Event` construction in `fire`
The code creates two `Event` objects per fire call: one for the guard evaluation loop, and one for the action/hooks.
Spec: **"One `data` dict holding the keyword arguments is created per call; every `Event` built during the call shares that same dict object"**
The code creates `shared_data = dict(data)`. Then it creates `Event(..., data=shared_data)`. This is correct.

### 6. `vending.py` Restock Validation
Spec: **"`restock(...)` | `maintenance` | Adds `qty` (≥ 1, else `ValueError`)... A new code needs a `price` (`KeyError` without one)"**
The code checks `qty < 1` and raises `ValueError`. It checks `if code not in products` and `if new_price is None` raises `KeyError`.
This logic is inside `restock_action`.

```python
    pass

    """Raised when all transitions for the event are rejected by guards."""

        self.state = state

            raise ValueError("states list is empty")

            if isinstance(s, str):
                state_obj = State(name=s)
            else:
                state_obj = s
            
            if state_obj.name in self._states:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate state name: {state_obj.name}")
            self._states[state_obj.name] = state_obj
        
        if initial not in self._states:
            raise ValueError(f"Initial state '{initial}' is not defined")
        
        self._initial = initial
        self.state = initial
        self.context = context
        self.history: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
        
        self._transitions: list[Transition] = []
        for t in transitions:
            # Validate source
            if t.source == '*':
                pass
            elif isinstance(t.source, (list, tuple)):
                for src in t.source:
                    if src not in self._states:
                        raise ValueError(f"Transition source '{src}' is not a state")
            elif isinstance(t.source, str):
                if t.source not in self._states:
                    raise ValueError(f"Transition source '{t.source}' is not a state")
            
            # Validate target
            if t.target is not None and t.target not in self._states:
                raise ValueError(f"Transition target '{t.target}' is not a state")
            
            self._transitions.append(t)
        
        self._listeners: list[callable] = []
        self._fire_depth = 0

    def _matches_source(self, trans: Transition, current_state: str) -> bool:
        if trans.source == '*':
            return True
        if isinstance(trans.source, str):
            return trans.source == current_state
        if isinstance(trans.source, (list, tuple)):
            return current_state in trans.source
        return False

    def fire(self, event_name: str, **data: Any) -> str:
        if self._fire_depth > 0:
            raise MachineError("Cannot call fire recursively")
        
        self._fire_depth += 1
        try:
            # Find candidates
            candidates = [
                t for t in self._transitions
                if t.event == event_name and self._matches_source(t, self.state)
            ]
            
            if not candidates:
                raise InvalidTransition(self.state, event_name)
            
            # Create shared data dict for all Events in this call
            shared_data = dict(data)
            
            # Find first candidate that passes guard
            selected_transition = None
            for t in candidates:
                # Determine target for guard evaluation
                # For guard, target is the current state (or target if normal)
                # But spec says: target is state transition leads to (for internal, current state)

                if t.target is None:
                    resolved_target = self.state
                else:
                    resolved_target = t.target

                    name=event_name,
                    source=self.state,
                    target=resolved_target,
                    data=shared_data
                )

                    selected_transition = t
                    break

                raise GuardRejected(self.state, event_name)

            current_state_name = self.state

                is_internal = True
            else:
                new_state_name = t.target
                is_internal = False

            # source is current state, target is the resolved target
            ev = Event(
                name=event_name,
                source=current_state_name,
                target=new_state_name,
                data=shared_data
            )
            
            if is_internal:
                # Internal transition
                # 1. Run action
                if t.action:
                    t.action(self, ev)
                
                # 2. Record history
                self.history.append((current_state_name, event_name, current_state_name))
                
                # 3. Call listeners
                for listener in self._listeners:
                    listener(current_state_name, ev, current_state_name)

                return current_state_name
            else:

                # 1. Run on_exit of current state
                source_state = self._states[current_state_name]
                if source_state.on_exit:
                    source_state.on_exit(self, ev)
                
                # 2. Run transition action
                if t.action:
                    t.action(self, ev)
                
                # 3. Set new state and record history
                self.state = new_state_name
                self.history.append((current_state_name, event_name, new_state_name))
                
                # 4. Run on_enter of new state
                target_state = self._states[new_state_name]
                if target_state.on_enter:
                    target_state.on_enter(self, ev)
                
                # 5. Call listeners
                for listener in self._listeners:
                    listener(current_state_name, ev, new_state_name)
                
                return new_state_name
                
        finally:
            self._fire_depth -= 1

    def can_fire(self, event_name: str, **data: Any) -> bool:
        # Find candidates
        candidates = [
            t for t in self._transitions
            if t.event == event_name and self._matches_source(t, self.state)
        ]
        
        if not candidates:
            return False
        
        shared_data = dict(data)
        
        for t in candidates:
            if t.target is None:
                resolved_target = self.state
            else:
                resolved_target = t.target
            
            ev = Event(
                name=event_name,
                source=self.state,
                target=resolved_target,
                data=shared_data
            )
            
            if t.guard is None or t.guard(self, ev):
                return True
        
        return False

    def available_events(self) -> list[str]:
        events = set()
        for t in self._transitions:
            if self._matches_source(t, self.state):
                events.add(t.event)
        return sorted(events)

    def on_transition(self, listener: callable) -> None:
        self._listeners.append(listener)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.state = self._initial
        self.history = []
```

```python
            else:
```

```python
                source_state = self._states[current_state_name]
                if source_state.on_exit:
                    source_state.on_exit(self, ev)
                
                # 2. Run transition action
                if t.action:
                    t.action(self, ev)
                
                # 3. Set new state and record history
                self.state = new_state_name
                self.history.append((current_state_name, event_name, new_state_name))

                target_state = self._states[new_state_name]
                if target_state.on_enter:
                    target_state.on_enter(self, ev)
                
                # 5. Call listeners
                for listener in self._listeners:
                    listener(current_state_name, ev, new_state_name)
                
                return new_state_name
                
        finally:
            self._fire_depth -= 1

    def can_fire(self, event_name: str, **data: Any) -> bool:
        # Find candidates
        candidates = [
            t for t in self._transitions
            if t.event == event_name and self._matches_source(t, self.state)
        ]
        
        if not candidates:
            return False
        
        shared_data = dict(data)
        
        for t in candidates:
            if t.target is None:
                resolved_target = self.state
            else:
                resolved_target = t.target
            
            ev = Event(
                name=event_name,
                source=self.state,
                target=resolved_target,
                data=shared_data
            )
            
            if t.guard is None or t.guard(self, ev):
                return True
        
        return False

    def available_events(self) -> list[str]:
        events = set()
        for t in self._transitions:
            if self._matches_source(t, self.state):
                events.add(t.event)
        return sorted(events)

    def on_transition(self, listener: callable) -> None:
        self._listeners.append(listener)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.state = self._initial
```

```python
from enum import Enum
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional


class AccountType(Enum):
    ASSET = "asset"
    LIABILITY = "liability"
    EQUITY = "equity"
    INCOME = "income"
    EXPENSE = "expense"

    @property
    def is_debit_normal(self) -> bool:
        return self in (AccountType.ASSET, AccountType.EXPENSE)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Account:
    code: str
    name: str
    type: AccountType
    parent: Optional[str] = None


class Chart:
    def __init__(self):
        self._accounts: dict[str, Account] = {}
        self._children: dict[str, list[str]] = {}

    def add(self, code: str, name: str, type: str | AccountType, parent: Optional[str] = None) -> Account:
        # Validate code: non-empty string of digits
        if not isinstance(code, str) or not code or not code.isdigit():
            raise ValueError("Code must be a non-empty string of digits")

        # Validate type
        if isinstance(type, str):
            try:
                type = AccountType(type.lower())
            except ValueError:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown account type: {type}")
        elif not isinstance(type, AccountType):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid account type: {type}")

        # Check if code exists
        if code in self._accounts:
            raise ValueError(f"Account code '{code}' already exists")

        # Validate parent
        if parent is not None:
            if parent not in self._accounts:
                raise ValueError(f"Parent account '{parent}' does not exist")
            parent_account = self._accounts[parent]
            if parent_account.type != type:
                raise ValueError(f"Parent account '{parent}' has type {parent_account.type}, but child type is {type}")

        # Create account
        account = Account(code=code, name=name, type=type, parent=parent)
        self._accounts[code] = account

        # Update children map
        if parent is not None:
            if parent not in self._children:
                self._children[parent] = []
            self._children[parent].append(code)

        return account

    def get(self, code: str) -> Account:
        if code not in self._accounts:
            raise KeyError(f"Account '{code}' not found")
        return self._accounts[code]

    def children(self, code: str) -> list[Account]:
        if code not in self._accounts:
            raise KeyError(f"Account '{code}' not found")
        
        child_codes = self._children.get(code, [])
        # Sort by code
        child_codes = sorted(child_codes)
        return [self._accounts[c] for c in child_codes]

    def roots(self) -> list[Account]:
        root_codes = [code for code, acc in self._accounts.items() if acc.parent is None]
        root_codes.sort()
        return [self._accounts[c] for c in root_codes]

    def is_leaf(self, code: str) -> bool:
        if code not in self._accounts:
            raise KeyError(f"Account '{code}' not found")
        return code not in self._children or not self._children[code]

    def walk(self) -> list[tuple[Account, int]]:
        result = []
        
        def dfs(code: str, depth: int):
            account = self._accounts[code]
            result.append((account, depth))
            # Get children sorted by code
            child_codes = sorted(self._children.get(code, []))
            for child_code in child_codes:
                dfs(child_code, depth + 1)

        root_codes = sorted([code for code, acc in self._accounts.items() if acc.parent is None])
        for root_code in root_codes:
            dfs(root_code, 0)
            
        return result
```

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta
import datetime
from typing import Callable

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    max_loans: int
    loan_days: int
    renewals: int
    daily_fine: int
    fine_cap: int
    grace_days: int

POLICY: dict[str, Policy] = {
    "standard": Policy(5, 21, 2, 25, 1000, 0),
    "student": Policy(3, 14, 1, 10, 500, 2),
    "staff": Policy(10, 42, 3, 0, 0, 0),
}

HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS = 3

def due_date(start: date, days: int) -> date:
    result = start + timedelta(days=days)
    # Sunday is weekday 6
    if result.weekday() == 6:
        result += timedelta(days=1)
    return result

def fine_for(kind: str, due: date, returned: date) -> int:
    if kind not in POLICY:
        raise KeyError(kind)
    policy = POLICY[kind]
    late = (returned - due).days
    if late <= policy.grace_days:
        return 0
    fine = late * policy.daily_fine
    if fine > policy.fine_cap:
        return policy.fine_cap
    return fine
```

```python
    def __init__(self):
        self._books: dict[str, Book] = {}
        self._members: dict[str, Member] = {}

    def add_book(self, isbn: str, title: str, author: str, copies: int = 1) -> Book:
        if isbn in self._books:
            raise ValueError(f"Book with ISBN {isbn} already exists")
        if copies < 1:
            raise ValueError("Copies must be at least 1")
        book = Book(isbn, title, author, copies)
        self._books[isbn] = book
        return book

    def add_copies(self, isbn: str, n: int) -> int:
        if isbn not in self._books:
            raise KeyError(isbn)
        if n < 1:
            raise ValueError("n must be at least 1")
        book = self._books[isbn]
        book.copies += n
        return book.copies

    def add_member(self, member_id: str, name: str, kind: str = 'standard') -> Member:
        from .fines import POLICY
        if member_id in self._members:
            raise ValueError(f"Member with ID {member_id} already exists")
        if kind not in POLICY:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid member kind: {kind}")
        member = Member(member_id, name, kind)
        self._members[member_id] = member
        return member

    def book(self, isbn: str) -> Book:
        if isbn not in self._books:
            raise KeyError(isbn)
        return self._books[isbn]

    def member(self, member_id: str) -> Member:
        if member_id not in self._members:
            raise KeyError(member_id)
        return self._members[member_id]

    def search(self, text: str) -> list[Book]:
        text_lower = text.lower()
        results = [
            book for book in self._books.values()
            if text_lower in book.title.lower() or text_lower in book.author.lower()
        ]
        results.sort(key=lambda b: (b.title, b.isbn))
        return results
```

```python
    def available(self, isbn: str) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        book = self.catalog.book(isbn)
        
        # Active loans
        active_loans_count = 0
        for loan in self._loans.values():
            if loan.isbn == isbn and loan.returned is None:

        # Ready holds
        ready_holds_count = 0
        if isbn in self._holds:

                    ready_holds_count += 1

    def checkout(self, member_id: str, isbn: str) -> Loan:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        # Check member exists
        member = self.catalog.member(member_id)
        # Check book exists
        self.catalog.book(isbn)
        
        # 1. Blocked if fine balance > 0
        bal = self._balances.get(member_id, 0)
        if bal > 0:
            raise Blocked(f"Member {member_id} has a balance of {bal} cents")
        
        # 2. DuplicateLoan if member already has this isbn on loan
        for loan in self._loans.values():
            if loan.member_id == member_id and loan.isbn == isbn and loan.returned is None:
                raise DuplicateLoan(f"Member {member_id} already has {isbn} on loan")
        
        # 3. LimitReached if member has max_loans active loans
        active_count = 0
        for loan in self._loans.values():
            if loan.member_id == member_id and loan.returned is None:
                active_count += 1
        
        policy = POLICY[member.kind]
        if active_count >= policy.max_loans:
            raise LimitReached(f"Member {member_id} has reached max loans ({policy.max_loans})")
        
        today = self.clock()
        
        # 4. Check holds
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            self._holds[isbn] = []
        
        holds_list = self._holds[isbn]
        
        # Check if member has a ready hold
        use_hold_copy = False
        hold_to_remove_idx = None
        
        for i, h in enumerate(holds_list):
            if h.member_id == member_id and h.status == 'ready':
                use_hold_copy = True
                hold_to_remove_idx = i
                break
        
        if not use_hold_copy:
            # Check if available
            if self.available(isbn) <= 0:
                raise NotAvailable(f"No copies of {isbn} available")
        else:
            # Remove the ready hold
            del holds_list[hold_to_remove_idx]
            # Does the freed copy (from the hold) become available?
            # No, it is being used by this checkout.
            # The hold was occupying a copy. That copy is now going out.
            # Effectively, the "available" count for others was reduced by this ready hold.
            # By removing it and using the copy, the state is consistent.
            
        # If the member had a WAITING hold, remove it now that they are checking out.
        # "A successful checkout also removes the member's waiting hold on the isbn, if any."
        if not use_hold_copy:
            for i, h in enumerate(holds_list):

                    break

            # The spec says place_hold raises DuplicateLoan if they already have a hold.

            pass

        self._loan_counter += 1
        loan_id = self._loan_counter
        
        due = due_date(today, policy.loan_days)
        
        loan = Loan(
            loan_id=loan_id,
            member_id=member_id,
            isbn=isbn,
            start=today,
            due=due
        )
        self._loans[loan_id] = loan
        return loan

    def place_hold(self, member_id: str, isbn: str) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        self.catalog.book(isbn)
        
        # DuplicateLoan if already on loan or already has hold
        for loan in self._loans.values():
            if loan.member_id == member_id and loan.isbn == isbn and loan.returned is None:
                raise DuplicateLoan(f"Member {member_id} already has {isbn} on loan")
        
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            self._holds[isbn] = []
            
        holds_list = self._holds[isbn]
        for h in holds_list:

                raise DuplicateLoan(f"Member {member_id} already has a hold on {isbn}")
        
        # LoanError if available(isbn) > 0
        if self.available(isbn) > 0:
            raise LoanError(f"Book {isbn} is currently available")
        
        # Add to end
        h = _Hold(member_id=member_id, status='waiting')
        holds_list.append(h)
        
        return len(holds_list)

    def cancel_hold(self, member_id: str, isbn: str) -> None:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        self.catalog.book(isbn)
        
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            raise KeyError("No hold found")
            
        holds_list = self._holds[isbn]
        found_idx = -1
        for i, h in enumerate(holds_list):
            if h.member_id == member_id:
                found_idx = i
                break
        
        if found_idx == -1:
            raise KeyError("No hold found")
        
        hold = holds_list[found_idx]
        
        if hold.status == 'ready':
            # Remove hold
            del holds_list[found_idx]
            
            # Pass copy on: next waiting hold becomes ready
            # Search from found_idx (now the next element) onwards for a waiting hold
            for i in range(found_idx, len(holds_list)):
                if holds_list[i].status == 'waiting':
                    holds_list[i].status = 'ready'
                    holds_list[i].deadline = self.clock() + timedelta(days=HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS)
                    break
        else:
            # Just remove waiting hold
            del holds_list[found_idx]

    def holds(self, isbn: str) -> list[str]:
        self._ensure_processed()
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            return []
        return [h.member_id for h in self._holds[isbn]]

    def hold_status(self, member_id: str, isbn: str):
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            raise KeyError("No hold found")
            
        holds_list = self._holds[isbn]
        for i, h in enumerate(holds_list):
            if h.member_id == member_id:
                if h.status == 'ready':
                    return ('ready', h.deadline)
                else:
                    return ('waiting', i + 1)
                    
        raise KeyError("No hold found")

    def renew(self, loan_id: int) -> date:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        if loan_id not in self._loans:
            raise KeyError(loan_id)
            
        loan = self._loans[loan_id]
        
        if loan.returned is not None:
            raise LoanError("Loan already returned")
            
        today = self.clock()
        
        # Check RenewalRefused conditions
        
        # 1. Overdue
        if today > loan.due:
            raise RenewalRefused("Loan is overdue")
            
        # 2. Has any hold (waiting or ready)
        if loan.isbn in self._holds:
            if len(self._holds[loan.isbn]) > 0:
                raise RenewalRefused("Book has holds")
                
        # 3. Renewals used up
        member = self.catalog.member(loan.member_id)
        policy = POLICY[member.kind]
        if loan.renewals >= policy.renewals:
            raise RenewalRefused("No renewals remaining")
            
        # All good
        loan.renewals += 1
        new_due = due_date(loan.due, policy.loan_days)
        loan.due = new_due
        return new_due

    def checkin(self, loan_id: int) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        if loan_id not in self._loans:
            raise KeyError(loan_id)
            
        loan = self._loans[loan_id]
        
        if loan.returned is not None:
            raise LoanError("Loan already returned")
            
        today = self.clock()
        
        # Compute fine
        member = self.catalog.member(loan.member_id)
        fine = fine_for(member.kind, loan.due, today)
        
        # Update loan
        loan.returned = today
        loan.fine = fine
        
        # Update balance
        if fine > 0:
            current_bal = self._balances.get(member.member_id, 0)
            self._balances[member.member_id] = current_bal + fine
            
        # Handle holds: set aside copy for earliest waiting hold
        if loan.isbn in self._holds:
            holds_list = self._holds[loan.isbn]
            for h in holds_list:
                if h.status == 'waiting':
                    h.status = 'ready'
                    h.deadline = today + timedelta(days=HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS)
                    break
                    
        return fine

    def accrued_fine(self, loan_id: int) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        if loan_id not in self._loans:
            raise KeyError(loan_id)
            
        loan = self._loans[loan_id]
        
        if loan.returned is not None:
            return loan.fine
            
        member = self.catalog.member(loan.member_id)
        today = self.clock()
        return fine_for(member.kind, loan.due, today)

    def balance(self, member_id: str) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        return self._balances.get(member_id, 0)

    def pay(self, member_id: str, amount: int) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        
        if amount <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Amount must be positive")
            
        current_bal = self._balances.get(member_id, 0)
        
        if amount > current_bal:
            raise ValueError("Payment amount exceeds balance")
            
        self._balances[member_id] = current_bal - amount
        return current_bal - amount

    def loans(self, member_id: str) -> list[Loan]:
        self._ensure_processed()
        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        
        active = [
            loan for loan in self._loans.values()
            if loan.member_id == member_id and loan.returned is None
        ]
        
        active.sort(key=lambda l: (l.due, l.loan_id))
        return active

    def overdue(self) -> list[Loan]:
        self._ensure_processed()
        today = self.clock()
        
        active = [
            loan for loan in self._loans.values()
            if loan.returned is None and loan.due < today
        ]
        
        active.sort(key=lambda l: (l.due, l.loan_id))
        return active
```

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    max_loans: int
    loan_days: int
    renewals: int
    daily_fine: int
    fine_cap: int
    grace_days: int

POLICY: dict[str, Policy] = {
    "standard": Policy(5, 21, 2, 25, 1000, 0),
    "student": Policy(3, 14, 1, 10, 500, 2),
    "staff": Policy(10, 42, 3, 0, 0, 0),
}

HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS = 3

def due_date(start: date, days: int) -> date:
    result = start + timedelta(days=days)
    # Sunday is weekday 6
    if result.weekday() == 6:
        result += timedelta(days=1)
    return result

def fine_for(kind: str, due: date, returned: date) -> int:
    if kind not in POLICY:
        raise KeyError(kind)
    policy = POLICY[kind]
    late = (returned - due).days
    if late <= policy.grace_days:
        return 0
    fine = late * policy.daily_fine
    if fine > policy.fine_cap:
        return policy.fine_cap
    return fine
```

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta
from typing import Optional, Callable

from .fines import POLICY, due_date, fine_for, HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS
from .catalog import Catalog

class LoanError(Exception):
    pass

class Blocked(LoanError):
    pass

class DuplicateLoan(LoanError):
    pass

class LimitReached(LoanError):
    pass

class NotAvailable(LoanError):
    pass

class RenewalRefused(LoanError):
    pass

@dataclass
class Loan:
    loan_id: int
    member_id: str
    isbn: str
    start: date
    due: date
    renewals: int = 0
    returned: Optional[date] = None
    fine: int = 0

@dataclass
class _Hold:
    member_id: str
    status: str  # 'waiting' or 'ready'
    deadline: Optional[date] = None  # Only for ready holds

class Library:
    def __init__(self, catalog: Catalog, clock: Callable[[], date]):
        self.catalog = catalog
        self.clock = clock
        self._loan_counter = 0
        self._loans: dict[int, Loan] = {}
        self._holds: dict[str, list[_Hold]] = {}  # isbn -> list of holds
        self._balances: dict[str, int] = {}  # member_id -> balance in cents
        self._last_processed_date: Optional[date] = None

    def _ensure_processed(self):
        today = self.clock()
        if self._last_processed_date is None:
            self._last_processed_date = today
            return
        
        # If we are behind, process days sequentially to handle cascading expiries correctly
        if today > self._last_processed_date:
            current = self._last_processed_date + timedelta(days=1)
            while current <= today:
                expired_any = False
                for isbn in list(self._holds.keys()):
                    if not self._holds[isbn]:
                        continue
                    
                    holds = self._holds[isbn]
                    
                    # Check for holds that are ready and have passed their deadline (expired)
                    # A hold is ready until end of day D. Expires on D+1.
                    # So if deadline < current day, it has expired.
                    expired_indices = [
                        i for i, h in enumerate(holds)
                        if h.status == 'ready' and h.deadline is not None and h.deadline < current
                    ]
                    
                    if expired_indices:
                        expired_any = True
                        # Process expiration for this isbn. 
                        # "On the day after the deadline the hold is removed and its copy passes to the next waiting hold"
                        # We process them one by one. Removing a hold might make another waiting hold ready.
                        # That new ready hold has deadline current + HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS. 
                        # Since current is the day we are simulating, and deadline is > current, 
                        # it won't expire in this same day iteration unless HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS is 0 or negative (it's 3).
                        # So we just need to handle the immediate expirations.
                        
                        # Sort indices to remove to keep stable order if multiple expire same day? 
                        # The queue order is maintained. If H1 and H2 expire, H1 is removed, H2's position might shift?
                        # Actually, if H1 expires, it passes copy to next waiting. H2 is still there?
                        # If H1 and H2 are both ready and expire, they are independent.
                        # "its copy passes to the next waiting hold".
                        # If H1 expires, copy goes to next waiting. H2 is Ready, so not waiting. Skipped.
                        # If H2 expires, copy goes to next waiting.
                        # If we remove H1 first, the "next waiting" relative to H1's position might include H2 if H2 were waiting?
                        # But H2 is ready.
                        # The cascade logic:
                        # "whenever the library looks at today's date, it first applies every expiry... in date order"
                        # This implies we apply the state change for day `current`.
                        
                        # Let's process the holds in order. 
                        # We need to remove expired ones and assign their copies to subsequent waiting holds.
                        # Since the queue order matters, we iterate from the beginning.
                        
                        new_holds = []
                        # We need to be careful: removing a hold might make a later hold ready?
                        # No, ready holds don't become waiting.
                        # Expired holds are removed. Their "copies" are passed to the *next* waiting hold in the queue.
                        
                        # Let's just filter out expired ones, and for each one, find the next waiting in the *original* queue?
                        # "pass to the next waiting hold".
                        # If H1(Ready, Exp), H2(Ready, Exp), H3(Waiting).
                        # H1 expires. Pass to next waiting. H2 is Ready, so skip. H3 is Waiting. H3 becomes Ready.
                        # H2 expires. Pass to next waiting. H3 is now Ready. So no waiting? 
                        # If H3 became Ready, it consumes the copy.
                        # So we should probably process cascades?
                        # "applies every expiry that should have happened by then, in date order"
                        # This usually implies we treat the day as a unit.
                        # If multiple copies are released, they go to the first N waiting holds.
                        
                        # Let's count how many copies are freed.
                        num_freed = len(expired_indices)
                        
                        # Remove expired holds
                        remaining_holds = [h for i, h in enumerate(holds) if i not in expired_indices]
                        
                        # Now assign freed copies to waiting holds
                        for _ in range(num_freed):
                            # Find first waiting hold in remaining_holds
                            assigned = False
                            for h in remaining_holds:
                                if h.status == 'waiting':
                                    h.status = 'ready'
                                    h.deadline = current + timedelta(days=HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS)
                                    assigned = True
                                    break
                            if not assigned:
                                break # No more waiting holds, copies become available (handled by count)
                        
                        self._holds[isbn] = remaining_holds
                
                # If no holds existed or none expired, do nothing.
                # Note: We don't break the while loop here, we just move to next day.
                # But if `expired_any` was false, state hasn't changed for this day, 
                # so subsequent days will behave similarly unless new holds are added (which we can't know).
                # The spec says "result never depends on which days the library was used".
                # This sequential processing simulates the "job" running every day.
                
                self._last_processed_date = current
                current += timedelta(days=1)
        
        # Ensure last processed is today
        self._last_processed_date = today

    def available(self, isbn: str) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        book = self.catalog.book(isbn)
        
        # Active loans
        active_loans_count = 0
        for loan in self._loans.values():
            if loan.isbn == isbn and loan.returned is None:
                active_loans_count += 1
        
        # Ready holds
        ready_holds_count = 0
        if isbn in self._holds:
            for h in self._holds[isbn]:
                if h.status == 'ready':
                    ready_holds_count += 1
        
        return book.copies - active_loans_count - ready_holds_count

    def checkout(self, member_id: str, isbn: str) -> Loan:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        # Check member exists
        member = self.catalog.member(member_id)
        # Check book exists
        self.catalog.book(isbn)
        
        # 1. Blocked if fine balance > 0
        bal = self._balances.get(member_id, 0)
        if bal > 0:
            raise Blocked(f"Member {member_id} has a balance of {bal} cents")
        
        # 2. DuplicateLoan if member already has this isbn on loan
        for loan in self._loans.values():
            if loan.member_id == member_id and loan.isbn == isbn and loan.returned is None:
                raise DuplicateLoan(f"Member {member_id} already has {isbn} on loan")
        
        # 3. LimitReached if member has max_loans active loans
        active_count = 0
        for loan in self._loans.values():
            if loan.member_id == member_id and loan.returned is None:
                active_count += 1
        
        policy = POLICY[member.kind]
        if active_count >= policy.max_loans:
            raise LimitReached(f"Member {member_id} has reached max loans ({policy.max_loans})")
        
        today = self.clock()
        
        # 4. Check holds
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            self._holds[isbn] = []
        
        holds_list = self._holds[isbn]
        
        # Check if member has a ready hold
        use_hold_copy = False
        hold_to_remove_idx = None
        
        for i, h in enumerate(holds_list):
            if h.member_id == member_id and h.status == 'ready':
                use_hold_copy = True
                hold_to_remove_idx = i
                break
        
        if not use_hold_copy:
            # Check if available
            if self.available(isbn) <= 0:
                raise NotAvailable(f"No copies of {isbn} available")
        
        # Remove holds on this isbn for this member
        # 1. If we used a ready hold, remove it.
        # 2. "A successful checkout also removes the member's waiting hold on the isbn, if any."
        # Since a member can't have multiple holds (enforced by place_hold), we just need to remove 
        # any hold (ready or waiting) that matches.
        
        # Find and remove any hold for this member
        for i, h in enumerate(holds_list):
            if h.member_id == member_id:
                del holds_list[i]
                break
        
        # Create Loan
        self._loan_counter += 1
        loan_id = self._loan_counter
        
        due = due_date(today, policy.loan_days)
        
        loan = Loan(
            loan_id=loan_id,
            member_id=member_id,
            isbn=isbn,
            start=today,
            due=due
        )
        self._loans[loan_id] = loan
        return loan

    def place_hold(self, member_id: str, isbn: str) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        self.catalog.book(isbn)
        
        # DuplicateLoan if already on loan or already has hold
        for loan in self._loans.values():
            if loan.member_id == member_id and loan.isbn == isbn and loan.returned is None:
                raise DuplicateLoan(f"Member {member_id} already has {isbn} on loan")
        
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            self._holds[isbn] = []
            
        holds_list = self._holds[isbn]
        for h in holds_list:
            if h.member_id == member_id:
                raise DuplicateLoan(f"Member {member_id} already has a hold on {isbn}")
        
        # LoanError if available(isbn) > 0
        if self.available(isbn) > 0:
            raise LoanError(f"Book {isbn} is currently available")
        
        # Add to end
        h = _Hold(member_id=member_id, status='waiting')
        holds_list.append(h)
        
        return len(holds_list)

    def cancel_hold(self, member_id: str, isbn: str) -> None:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        self.catalog.book(isbn)
        
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            raise KeyError("No hold found")
            
        holds_list = self._holds[isbn]
        found_idx = -1
        for i, h in enumerate(holds_list):
            if h.member_id == member_id:
                found_idx = i
                break
        
        if found_idx == -1:
            raise KeyError("No hold found")
        
        hold = holds_list[found_idx]
        
        if hold.status == 'ready':
            # Remove hold
            del holds_list[found_idx]
            
            # Pass copy on: next waiting hold becomes ready
            # "Cancelling a ready hold passes its copy on as if it had expired today: 
            # the next waiting hold becomes ready with deadline today + HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS."
            today = self.clock()
            # Search from found_idx (which is now the index of the next element) onwards
            for i in range(found_idx, len(holds_list)):
                if holds_list[i].status == 'waiting':
                    holds_list[i].status = 'ready'
                    holds_list[i].deadline = today + timedelta(days=HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS)
                    break
        else:
            # Just remove waiting hold
            del holds_list[found_idx]

    def holds(self, isbn: str) -> list[str]:
        self._ensure_processed()
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            return []
        return [h.member_id for h in self._holds[isbn]]

    def hold_status(self, member_id: str, isbn: str):
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        if isbn not in self._holds:
            raise KeyError("No hold found")
            
        holds_list = self._holds[isbn]
        for i, h in enumerate(holds_list):
            if h.member_id == member_id:
                if h.status == 'ready':
                    return ('ready', h.deadline)
                else:
                    return ('waiting', i + 1)
                    
        raise KeyError("No hold found")

    def renew(self, loan_id: int) -> date:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        if loan_id not in self._loans:
            raise KeyError(loan_id)
            
        loan = self._loans[loan_id]
        
        if loan.returned is not None:
            raise LoanError("Loan already returned")
            
        today = self.clock()
        
        # Check RenewalRefused conditions
        
        # 1. Overdue
        if today > loan.due:
            raise RenewalRefused("Loan is overdue")
            
        # 2. Has any hold (waiting or ready)
        if loan.isbn in self._holds:
            if len(self._holds[loan.isbn]) > 0:
                raise RenewalRefused("Book has holds")
                
        # 3. Renewals used up
        member = self.catalog.member(loan.member_id)
        policy = POLICY[member.kind]
        if loan.renewals >= policy.renewals:
            raise RenewalRefused("No renewals remaining")
            
        # All good
        loan.renewals += 1
        new_due = due_date(loan.due, policy.loan_days)
        loan.due = new_due
        return new_due

    def checkin(self, loan_id: int) -> int:
        self._ensure_processed()
        
        if loan_id not in self._loans:
            raise KeyError(loan_id)
            
        loan = self._loans[loan_id]
        
        if loan.returned is not None:
            raise LoanError("Loan already returned")
            
        today = self.clock()
        
        # Compute fine
        member = self.catalog.member(loan.member_id)
        fine = fine_for(member.kind, loan.due, today)
        
        # Update loan
        loan.returned = today
        loan.fine = fine
        
        # Update balance
        if fine > 0:
            current_bal = self._balances.get(member.member_id, 0)
            self._balances[member.member_id] = current_bal + fine
            
        # Handle holds: set aside copy for earliest waiting hold
        # "sets the copy aside for a waiting hold if there is one"
        if loan.isbn in self._holds:
            holds_list = self._holds[loan.isbn]
            for h in holds_list:
                if h.status == 'waiting':
                    h.status = 'ready'
                    h.deadline = today + timedelta(days=HOLD_PICKUP_DAYS)
                    break
                    
        return fine

    def accrued_fine(self, loan_id: int) -> int:

            raise KeyError(loan_id)
            
        loan = self._loans[loan_id]

            return loan.fine
            
        member = self.catalog.member(loan.member_id)
        today = self.clock()
        return fine_for(member.kind, loan.due, today)

    def balance(self, member_id: str) -> int:

        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        return self._balances.get(member_id, 0)

        self.catalog.member(member_id)

        if amount > current_bal:
            raise ValueError("Payment amount exceeds balance")
            
        self._balances[member_id] = current_bal - amount
        return current_bal - amount

    def loans(self, member_id: str) -> list[Loan]:
        self._ensure_processed()
        self.catalog.member(member_id)
        
        active = [
            loan for loan in self._loans.values()
            if loan.member_id == member_id and loan.returned is None
        ]

            loan for loan in self._loans.values()
            if loan.returned is None and loan.due < today
        ]
        
        active.sort(key=lambda l: (l.due, l.loan_id))
        return active
```

```python
        result += timedelta(days=1)
    return result

def fine_for(kind: str, due: date, returned: date) -> int:
    if kind not in POLICY:
        raise KeyError(kind)
    policy = POLICY[kind]
    late = (returned - due).days
    if late <= policy.grace_days:
        return 0
    fine = late * policy.daily_fine
    if fine > policy.fine_cap:
        return policy.fine_cap
    return fine
```

```python
            raise KeyError(isbn)
        if n < 1:
            raise ValueError("n must be at least 1")
        book = self._books[isbn]
        book.copies += n
        return book.copies

    def add_member(self, member_id: str, name: str, kind: str = 'standard') -> Member:
        from .fines import POLICY
        if member_id in self._members:
            raise ValueError(f"Member with ID {member_id} already exists")
        if kind not in POLICY:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid member kind: {kind}")
        member = Member(member_id, name, kind)
        self._members[member_id] = member
        return member

            raise KeyError(isbn)
        return self._books[isbn]

    def member(self, member_id: str) -> Member:
        if member_id not in self._members:
            raise KeyError(member_id)
        return self._members[member_id]

    def search(self, text: str) -> list[Book]:
        text_lower = text.lower()
        results = [
            book for book in self._books.values()
            if text_lower in book.title.lower() or text_lower in book.author.lower()
        ]
        results.sort(key=lambda b: (b.title, b.isbn))
```
