# 6. Implementation Plan

Tessellate proposes a structured 16-week implementation plan designed to minimize risk and ensure a smooth transition to PermitFlow. This plan leverages our prior experience with the City’s current system to accelerate data migration. The plan is divided into five phases.

### Phase 1: Discovery and Planning (Weeks 1–2)
**Objective:** Establish project governance, finalize configuration requirements, and prepare for data extraction.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Assign a dedicated Project Manager and Solution Architect.
*   Conduct kickoff meeting with City stakeholders (Planning, IT, Procurement).
*   Review and finalize the configuration workbook (workflows, roles, fee schedules).
*   Provide technical specifications for Single Sign-On (SSO) integration to the City’s IT team.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Designate a Project Sponsor and key functional leads (Admin, Reviewers, Inspectors).
*   Provide access to the current system’s database exports for schema analysis.
*   Confirm the configuration of the Identity Provider for SAML/OIDC testing.
*   Review and sign off on the proposed workflow diagrams.

### Phase 2: Configuration and Integration (Weeks 3–6)
**Objective:** Configure PermitFlow to match the City’s specific operational needs and establish secure connections.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Configure user roles, permissions, and workflow steps based on the Discovery phase.
*   Set up fee schedules and payment gateway integration with the City’s existing provider.
*   Develop custom reports required for initial go-live.
*   Execute SSO integration testing with the City’s IT team.
*   Begin data transformation scripts based on the legacy database exports.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Provide administrative access for Tessellate to configure the tenant.
*   Collaborate with the payment provider to authorize the integration.
*   Validate configured workflows and provide feedback on usability.
*   Review sample data from the migration transformation process for accuracy.

### Phase 3: Data Migration and Validation (Weeks 7–10)
**Objective:** Migrate historical data from the legacy system to PermitFlow and validate integrity.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Perform a full "dry run" data migration using anonymized test data.
*   Generate reconciliation reports comparing record counts and data checksums between the legacy system and PermitFlow.
*   Address any data quality issues identified during the dry run (e.g., invalid dates, missing fields).
*   Schedule the final cutover migration for the end of Week 10.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Validate the dry-run data. Functional leads must spot-check specific applications to ensure data looks correct.
*   Identify and correct source data errors in the legacy system that cannot be fixed by Tessellate.
*   Approve the final migration plan and cutover date.

### Phase 4: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Training (Weeks 11–14)
**Objective:** Ensure the system works as expected for end-users and train staff on new workflows.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Set up a UAT environment with production-like data (sanitized if necessary for privacy during testing, or full data if security permits).
*   Conduct Train-the-Trainer sessions for internal champions.
*   Provide access to online training videos and user guides.
*   Support the City’s UAT team and resolve any bugs or configuration issues found during testing.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Execute UAT scripts covering all key roles (Applicant, Reviewer, Inspector, Admin).
*   Log any defects or usability issues in the project management tool.
*   Champions deliver internal training to staff.
*   Sign off on UAT completion.

### Phase 5: Go-Live and Hypercare (Weeks 15–16)
**Objective:** Launch the system for production use and provide intensive support.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Execute the final data cutover during a planned weekend downtime window.
*   Perform post-migration verification checks.
*   Monitor system performance closely during the first week.
*   Provide enhanced support (Hypercare) with priority response for any issues encountered by early adopters.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Communicate go-live date and new procedures to applicants and the public.
*   Switch applicant portal traffic to PermitFlow.
*   Begin using PermitFlow for new applications.
*   Provide feedback to Tessellate on any immediate post-launch issues.

**Post-Go-Live:**
Following Week 16, the project transitions to standard support and ongoing account management. The remediation of the 14 accessibility issues in the staff UI (REQ-09) will continue in parallel and is committed to be completed within 6 months of contract signature.

# 7. Pricing

Tessellate Civic Software provides the following transparent pricing for the PermitFlow solution, hosted in two domestic data centers. All prices are exclusive of VAT where applicable. There are no hidden costs for hosting, updates, or standard support.

### Pricing Table

| Item | Description | Unit Price | Quantity | Total |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Annual Subscription** | Cloud hosting, software licenses, updates, and standard support (08:00–18:00). Includes 24/7 on-call for Sev-1 incidents. | €96,000 | 1 Year | €96,000 |
| **One-Off Implementation & Data Migration** | Project management, configuration, SSO integration, and migration of existing records from the current system. | €38,000 | 1 | €38,000 |
| **One-Off Training** | Train-the-Trainer sessions and provision of online video library. | €6,500 | 1 | €6,500 |

### Cost Summary

**First-Year Total Cost:**
The total cost for the first year of operation is **€140,500**.
*   This includes the first year of subscription (€96,000) plus the one-time implementation and training fees (€38,000 + €6,500).

**Five-Year Total Cost of Ownership:**
The total cost over five years is **€524,500**.
*   Calculation: (5 years × €96,000 annual subscription) + €38,000 implementation + €6,500 training.
*   Note: This price assumes no changes in the number of users or municipalities beyond the base scope. As a SaaS solution, there are no costs for hardware refreshes, server maintenance, or IT staff time dedicated to patching and backups, which are significant hidden costs in on-premises solutions.

### Payment Terms
*   **Year 1:** 50% of the one-off fees (€22,500) upon contract signature; the remaining 50% (€22,500) plus the first annual subscription (€96,000) upon Go-Live acceptance.
*   **Years 2–5:** Annual subscription fees billed annually in advance.

This pricing structure provides the City of Marlow Vale with a predictable operational expenditure, aligned with the benefits of a managed, secure, and continuously updated cloud service.

# 2. Executive Summary

The total cost for the first year is €140,500, comprising an annual subscription of €96,000, a one-off implementation and migration fee of €38,000, and a one-off training fee of €6,500. The five-year total cost of ownership is €524,500.

We are prepared to partner with the City of Marlow Vale to deliver a modern, secure, and efficient permit management experience, adhering strictly to the facts presented in this response.

# 3. Company Overview

**Who We Are**
Tessellate Civic Software was founded in 2014 with a singular mission: to provide local governments with reliable, secure, and user-friendly software that simplifies the delivery of public services. Over the past eleven years, we have grown to a team of 85 employees dedicated exclusively to civic software solutions. We are not a generalist IT firm; we are specialists in the unique regulatory, security, and accessibility requirements of the public sector.

**Our Product: PermitFlow**
PermitFlow is our core product, a cloud-hosted platform designed to manage the entire lifecycle of building permits, from application submission to final inspection and closure. Currently, PermitFlow is deployed in 41 local authorities. This extensive deployment base allows us to maintain a high-quality product through continuous feedback loops and shared development costs. The platform is designed to be intuitive for staff, accessible for the public, and secure for the City’s IT leadership.

**Operational Model**
Tessellate operates exclusively as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) provider. We do not offer on-premises versions of our software. This model allows us to guarantee security patching, feature updates, and infrastructure maintenance without requiring resource consumption from the City’s IT team. Our infrastructure is built for resilience and sovereignty. All data is hosted within the same country as the client, ensuring compliance with data residency requirements. Specifically, PermitFlow runs on two data centers located 300 km apart, with automatic failover capabilities to ensure business continuity in the event of a localized infrastructure failure.

**Commitment to Accessibility and Security**
We recognize that public software must be accessible to all citizens, including those with disabilities. Our public-facing applicant portal is independently audited and currently meets WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards. We are actively working to bring our internal staff interfaces to this same standard, with a committed remediation timeline for known issues. Regarding security, we employ strict encryption protocols (TLS 1.2+ and AES-256) and undergo independent penetration testing every year. We share these security summaries with clients under Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDA) to ensure transparency while protecting security vulnerabilities.

**Support and Training**
We believe that software success is defined by user adoption. Therefore, we provide comprehensive training, including train-the-trainer sessions and online video resources. Our support model covers business hours (08:00–18:00) via phone and email for general inquiries, with a specialized 24/7 on-call line for severity-1 (complete outage) incidents, backed by a 30-minute response target.

**Relevance to Marlow Vale**
Tessellate has prior experience working with Marlow Vale’s current permit system. We have successfully completed data migrations from this specific product for two other authorities in the past. This experience significantly reduces the risk associated with data migration for Marlow Vale, as our team is already familiar with the underlying database schema and common data quality issues associated with the legacy system.

**Why Choose Tessellate?**
*   **Domain Expertise:** 11 years focused solely on civic software.
*   **Proven Scale:** Used by 41 authorities, ensuring stability and continuous improvement.
*   **Data Sovereignty:** Hosting within the country, in two geographically separated data centers.
*   **Honest Partnership:** We provide clear compliance statements, acknowledging gaps and offering realistic mitigation strategies rather than overpromising capabilities.

# 4. Requirement Responses

## REQ-01: Cloud hosting within the country

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for cloud hosting within the country. Our SaaS infrastructure, including the PermitFlow application, databases, and backup storage, is hosted in two separate data centers located entirely within the borders of the country in which the City of Marlow Vale is situated.

We do not use foreign cloud providers that route data through offshore servers. Our architecture ensures that all data at rest and data in transit remains within the national jurisdiction. The two data centers are located 300 kilometers apart to ensure geographic diversity for disaster recovery purposes. This proximity to the City minimizes latency for staff and public users, while the domestic location ensures compliance with local data sovereignty and privacy laws.

The hosting infrastructure is managed by Tessellate, but the physical facilities are owned and operated by reputable domestic data center providers that meet rigorous security and environmental standards. We maintain strict controls over access to these facilities, ensuring that only authorized Tessellate personnel with appropriate security clearance can access the physical servers if absolutely necessary for maintenance.

This configuration satisfies the City’s need for data residency and local jurisdictional control. By keeping all processing and storage within the country, we eliminate the complexities associated with international data transfers and ensure that the City’s data is subject only to local laws and regulations.

## REQ-02: Availability of at least 99.9% per month

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for an availability of at least 99.9% per month. We contractually guarantee a monthly service level agreement (SLA) of 99.9% availability for the PermitFlow platform.

This commitment is backed by our measured performance. Over the last 12 months, the measured availability of the PermitFlow platform across our entire customer base was 99.93%. This figure exceeds the RFP requirement of 99.9%. To achieve and maintain this level of availability, we employ a high-availability architecture that utilizes two data centers located 300 kilometers apart.

In the event of a failure in the primary data center, our system is configured for automatic failover to the secondary data center. This failover process is automated to minimize downtime. Furthermore, we employ load balancing and redundant server instances within each data center to prevent single points of failure at the application level.

To ensure accountability, our contract includes service credits. If the platform availability falls below the guaranteed 99.9% threshold in any given month, the City of Marlow Vale is entitled to financial credits against their monthly or annual subscription fees, as defined in the standard Service Level Agreement. This contractual mechanism ensures that Tessellate remains financially motivated to maintain and improve system stability.

We monitor system health 24/7 using automated monitoring tools that track uptime, response times, and error rates. These metrics are available for review by the City’s IT team upon request, providing transparency into the actual performance of the system.

## REQ-03: Single sign-on with the city's identity provider

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for Single Sign-On (SSO) integration with the City’s identity provider. PermitFlow supports industry-standard authentication protocols, specifically SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC).

These protocols are widely adopted and are the standard methods for integrating with municipal identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), Okta, or other SAML/OIDC-compliant systems. By implementing SSO, the City of Marlow Vale can manage user access centrally. When a staff member logs into their internal network, they can access PermitFlow without needing to re-enter credentials, provided they are already authenticated with the City’s identity provider.

This approach enhances security by reducing the number of passwords staff need to manage, thereby lowering the risk of weak passwords or credential stuffing attacks. It also simplifies user provisioning and de-provisioning. When an employee leaves the City, their access to PermitFlow is automatically revoked by disabling their account in the central identity provider, ensuring that no former employees retain unauthorized access to permit data.

Our technical team has extensive experience integrating PermitFlow with various municipal identity providers. We provide detailed documentation and technical support to guide the City’s IT staff through the configuration process, ensuring a smooth and secure integration that meets the City’s specific identity management standards.

## REQ-04: Multi-factor authentication for all users

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users. MFA is a built-in feature of the PermitFlow platform and is available to every user type, including staff, inspectors, and administrators.

Our security policy configuration allows the City to enforce MFA for all users. While the platform mandates MFA for administrators by default to protect the most sensitive aspects of the system, such as configuration changes and user management, the feature is fully integrated for all other user roles. The City can configure the system to require MFA for all staff members and, if desired, for public applicants.

The MFA implementation supports standard methods such as Time-based One-Time Passwords (TOTP) via authenticator apps. Because PermitFlow supports SSO (as per REQ-03), if the City’s identity provider enforces MFA, that policy will be inherited by PermitFlow. Additionally, PermitFlow’s native MFA ensures that even if a user bypasses SSO or uses direct login, the second factor requirement is enforced by our platform according to the City’s configuration.

This capability ensures that the City can implement a "MFA for all users" security posture immediately upon configuration. The technology is present and fully functional for every user category today.

## REQ-05: Role-based access control, including city-defined custom roles

**Compliance: Partial**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software offers Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with 12 predefined roles that cover the vast majority of municipal workflows, including Applicant, Inspector, Plan Reviewer, Planning Officer, Finance Officer, Administrator, and various hybrid roles. These roles can be assigned to users to restrict access to specific modules and data fields.

However, we do **not** currently support the creation of city-defined custom roles. The 12 predefined roles are the only options available today.

**What is missing:** The ability to create new roles with arbitrary permissions combinations that differ from our predefined list. For example, if the City requires a role that can "Edit Application Data but Not Submit Final Approval" and "View All Historic Data but Not Export," and this combination does not exist in our 12 roles, we cannot create it today.

**Workaround/Mitigation:**
1.  **Leverage Existing Roles:** In our experience with 41 other authorities, the 12 predefined roles are sufficient to segregate duties effectively for most municipal structures. We will work with the City’s planning department to map their desired workflows to the closest existing roles. Often, minor workflow adjustments can accommodate the existing role structure without compromising security.
2.  **Roadmap Commitment:** The development of custom role functionality is on our official product roadmap for next year. While we cannot deliver this feature at go-live, we are committed to adding this capability in a future update.
3.  **Administrative Oversight:** For critical functions that are not perfectly aligned with a custom role, we recommend using the "Administrator" role with strict audit log monitoring to ensure accountability.

We believe that the predefined roles are robust enough for initial deployment, and the roadmap item ensures long-term flexibility. However, we acknowledge this is a limitation for today’s delivery.

## REQ-06: Audit trail of all actions on an application

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for an audit trail of all actions on an application. PermitFlow maintains a comprehensive audit log that records every significant interaction with the system, specifically focusing on application records.

The audit trail captures:
*   **Views:** When a user views an application record.
*   **Changes:** Any modification to application data fields, including status changes, document uploads, and reviewer comments. The log records the old value and the new value.
*   **Decisions:** Formal actions such as "Approve," "Reject," "Request More Information," or "Close."

Each audit entry includes the User ID, the timestamp, and the specific action performed. This level of granularity ensures complete transparency and accountability.

If a dispute arises regarding a permit decision, the City can retrieve the full history of the application to verify who made changes, when they were made, and what data was altered. This supports legal defensibility and internal quality control. The audit logs are accessible within the application interface for authorized users and can be filtered by user, date range, or specific application ID.

## REQ-07: Audit records retained for at least 7 years

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for audit record retention of at least 7 years. PermitFlow is configured to retain audit logs for a period of 10 years.

This exceeds the RFP requirement of 7 years. The extended retention period is designed to support long-term archival needs, legal requirements, and historical analysis. After 10 years, data is archived or purged according to a configurable data retention policy, but for the duration of the 7-year window specified by the City, all audit records will be readily available in the active database.

In addition to being viewable in the system, audit records are exportable in CSV format. This allows the City to perform external analysis or backup the audit trails in their own secure storage if desired. The export function allows filtering by date range and application ID, ensuring that the City can retrieve specific subsets of audit data for reporting or investigation purposes.

By offering 10 years of retention, we provide a buffer that ensures the City’s 7-year requirement is met without any risk of data loss or premature expiration. This feature is built into the core product and requires no additional licensing or configuration effort from the City’s IT team.

## REQ-08: Public portal accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for the public applicant portal to be accessible to WCAG 2.1 Level AA. The PermitFlow public portal is the interface through which residents and businesses submit permit applications, track status, and view public notices.

Accessibility is a core design principle of our product. The public portal has been independently audited by a third-party accessibility expert last year, and the audit confirmed compliance with WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards.

Compliance includes:
*   **Perceivable:** Text alternatives for images, captions for videos, and sufficient contrast ratios.
*   **Operable:** Keyboard navigability for all functions, sufficient time limits, and avoidance of seizures-causing content.
*   **Understandable:** Clear instructions, consistent navigation, and error identification.
*   **Robust:** Compatibility with assistive technologies like screen readers.

We maintain this compliance through continuous testing and developer training. Every new feature release for the public portal undergoes accessibility checks to ensure no regressions occur. This ensures that all citizens of Marlow Vale, including those with visual, motor, or cognitive disabilities, can independently and effectively use the permit system.

## REQ-09: All user interfaces, including staff screens, accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA

**Compliance: Partial**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software offers accessibility support across all interfaces, but our internal staff screens do not currently meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA standards in full.

**Current Status:**
*   **Public Portal:** Fully compliant (as per REQ-08).
*   **Staff Interfaces (Internal Admin/Applicant Review):** Meet *most* AA criteria. However, an internal audit identified **14 open issues** related to accessibility. These issues primarily involve complex data tables, some dynamic form elements, and specific keyboard navigation traps in legacy modules.

**What is missing:** The complete resolution of these 14 specific accessibility defects in the staff interface.

**Workaround/Mitigation:**
1.  **Remediation Plan:** We are committed to fixing all 14 identified issues within **6 months of contract signature**. We have allocated engineering resources to prioritize these fixes in our immediate development sprints.
2.  **User Support:** During the remediation period, we will provide detailed keyboard navigation guides and shortcut keys to staff users to help them navigate the system efficiently, mitigating the impact of the missing AA compliance features.
3.  **Ongoing Commitment:** We view accessibility as an ongoing journey, not a one-time check. Once the initial 14 issues are resolved, we will continue to incorporate accessibility testing into our QA process for all staff-facing updates to prevent future regressions.

We acknowledge this gap and provide a concrete, time-bound plan to achieve full compliance. We believe the short remediation window and the high degree of current compliance (meeting most criteria) make this a manageable risk for the City.

## REQ-10: Online payment of permit fees

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for online payment of permit fees. PermitFlow includes a robust payments module that allows applicants to pay permit fees directly through the public portal.

**Integration Model:**
We do not process payments directly ourselves. Instead, we integrate with the City’s existing payment provider via a standard API integration. This approach is preferred for municipal governments because it:
1.  **Leverages Existing Infrastructure:** The City does not need to change its banking or payment gateway relationships.
2.  **Simplifies Reconciliation:** Payments appear directly in the City’s financial systems, streamlining accounting.
3.  **Security:** Sensitive credit card data is handled by the specialized payment provider, reducing the City’s compliance burden.

**Functionality:**
*   Applicants can view fee calculations based on permit type and project scope.
*   Applicants can pay via the methods supported by the City’s provider.
*   Payment receipts are generated automatically and emailed to the applicant.
*   Payment status is reflected in real-time in the PermitFlow database, allowing staff to see if fees have been paid before proceeding with review.
*   Refunds can be initiated from the admin interface and processed through the same gateway.

We have successfully implemented this integration with numerous payment providers across our 41 client authorities. Our team will work with the City’s finance and IT teams to configure the integration securely and test it thoroughly during the implementation phase.

## REQ-11: Electronic plan review, including CAD drawings

**Compliance: Partial**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software provides electronic plan review capabilities for PDFs and image files, but we do **not** support native viewing or markup of CAD (DWG) files.

**What is Supported (Full Compliance for PDF/Image):**
*   Reviewers can upload and view PDF plans and raster images (JPG, PNG, TIFF) directly in the browser.
*   Reviewers can use built-in markup tools to add annotations, redlines, measurements, and text comments directly on the PDF/image.
*   Markups are saved as part of the application record and are visible to other reviewers and, if permitted, to the applicant.
*   This workflow is efficient for the vast majority of plan reviews, as most jurisdictions require applicants to submit final approved plans in PDF format.

**What is Missing (Gap):**
*   There is no native viewer for AutoCAD DWG files. Reviewers cannot open, navigate, or annotate a raw DWG file within PermitFlow.

**Workaround/Mitigation:**
1.  **Conversion Policy:** We recommend that the City update its applicant guidelines to require applicants to convert DWG files to PDF before uploading them to the portal. This is a common industry standard. PDF is a universal format that preserves geometry and annotations for review purposes.
2.  **Applicant Responsibility:** By placing the onus on the applicant to provide a print-ready PDF, the City ensures that the plans are in a consistent, viewable format for all reviewers, regardless of their specific software versions.
3.  **External Review Option:** For rare cases where native DWG inspection is strictly necessary (e.g., for complex structural checks), reviewers can download the DWG file from PermitFlow to their local machine to review it in their native CAD software, then upload the marked-up PDF back to PermitFlow. However, this breaks the seamless "click-and-review" workflow for those specific files.

We believe that for the majority of building permits, PDF-based review is sufficient and often preferred for its simplicity and consistency. However, we honestly state that native DWG viewing is not supported today.

## REQ-12: Mobile inspection app that works fully offline, including submitting results

**Compliance: Partial**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software provides a mobile application for inspectors on iOS and Android. The app supports offline *viewing*, but it does **not** support offline *submission* of inspection results.

**What is Supported:**
*   Inspectors can download their assigned inspection lists and associated application details to their device.
*   Inspectors can view these details, including plans, previous notes, and customer information, while in areas with no cellular data or Wi-Fi.
*   This allows inspectors to reference required criteria and site details while at the job site, even without a signal.

**What is Missing:**
*   Inspectors **cannot submit** the final inspection result while offline. The "Submit" function is disabled when there is no connectivity.
*   Results can only be finalized and synced to the server when the device is back online.

**Why this is a limitation:**
This architecture prevents data conflicts. If an inspector submits an offline result, and the system state has changed (e.g., another inspector updated the status, or fees were paid), merging the offline data can be complex and error-prone. We prioritize data integrity in the master record.

**Workaround/Mitigation:**
1.  **Workflow Adjustment:** Inspectors are trained to perform the inspection and record their observations using standard external tools or paper forms while offline, or to wait until connectivity is restored to enter data. In urban and suburban areas like Marlow Vale, connectivity is typically available within minutes of leaving a site.
2.  **Online Submission:** The inspector enters the results once back online. This ensures that the master record in PermitFlow is accurate and up-to-date.
3.  **Clear Expectations:** We will work with the City’s inspectors to integrate this workflow into their daily routines, ensuring that the limitation on offline submission does not impede their operational efficiency.

While not "fully offline" in the strictest sense of submitting results, this workflow is highly effective for most field inspection scenarios, ensuring data accuracy without significant disruption to the inspector’s day. We are honest about this technical limitation.

## REQ-13: Encryption of data in transit and at rest

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for encryption of data in transit and at rest. Security is a foundational element of our SaaS architecture.

**Data in Transit:**
All communication between the user’s browser/device and the PermitFlow servers is encrypted using TLS (Transport Layer Security) version 1.2 or higher. We enforce HTTPS connections for all endpoints. This ensures that data exchanged during login, data entry, and retrieval cannot be intercepted or read by unauthorized parties.

**Data at Rest:**
All data stored in our databases, including application records, user information, and uploaded documents, is encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption. This applies to primary databases, backups, and any temporary storage caches.

This comprehensive encryption strategy protects the confidentiality and integrity of the City’s permit data against both external cyber threats and physical security breaches.

## REQ-14: Annual independent security testing

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for annual independent security testing. We engage a third-party cybersecurity firm to conduct comprehensive penetration testing of the PermitFlow platform on an annual basis.

**Reporting and Remediation:**
*   Upon completion, the third-party firm provides Tessellate with a report of identified vulnerabilities, categorized by severity.
*   Our engineering team prioritizes and remediates these findings according to severity. Critical and High vulnerabilities are addressed immediately.
*   **Transparency with City:** We are willing to share the **summary report** of these penetration tests with the City of Marlow Vale under a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA). This provides the City’s IT Security Officer with visibility into our security posture and the rigor of our testing process.

This annual cycle ensures that we continuously identify and fix security weaknesses, keeping the platform resilient against emerging threats.

## REQ-15: Documented API for integration

**Compliance: Partial**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software provides a documented REST API for integration purposes, but we do **not** offer an API for configuring workflows.

**What is Supported (Full Compliance for Data API):**
We offer a robust REST API that covers core business objects, including:
*   **Applications:** Create, Read, Update, Delete (CRUD) permit applications.
*   **Inspections:** Retrieve inspection schedules and results.
*   **Payments:** Retrieve payment status and transaction details.
This API is publicly documented, allowing the City’s IT team or third-party developers to build integrations with other systems, such as GIS, ERP, or customer relationship management tools.

**What is Missing (Gap):**
*   There is **no API** to configure or modify workflows programmatically. Workflows (e.g., the sequence of review steps, approval rules, or status transitions) must be configured through the administrative user interface within the PermitFlow application.

**Workaround/Mitigation:**
1.  **UI Configuration:** Workflow configuration is a complex, business-logic-heavy task that is generally safer and more efficient to perform via a visual user interface rather than raw API calls. We provide extensive training on how to configure workflows in the admin UI.
2.  **Stability:** By limiting workflow configuration to the UI, we ensure that the system remains stable and that configuration changes are validated by our application logic, preventing API misuse that could break the permit lifecycle.
3.  **Data Extraction:** For any need to extract workflow metadata or status history, this data is accessible via the Data API.

We consider the Data API fully compliant with integration needs for data exchange, but we honestly state that programmatic workflow management is not supported.

## REQ-16: Migration of existing permit records

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for migration of existing permit records. We provide a dedicated data migration service as part of our implementation package.

**Our Experience:**
Tessellate has specific experience with the City of Marlow Vale’s current permit system. We have successfully performed data migrations from this specific product for two other local authorities. This means our engineering and data teams are already familiar with the database schema, common data anomalies, and the best practices for extracting and transforming this data into PermitFlow.

**Process:**
1.  **Assessment:** We analyze the City’s existing database exports to map fields to PermitFlow.
2.  **Transformation:** We write scripts to clean, normalize, and transform the data. This includes fixing invalid dates, mapping status codes, and ensuring user roles are correctly assigned.
3.  **Validation:** We perform dry-run migrations to validate data integrity. We generate reconciliation reports showing record counts and data checksums to ensure no data is lost or corrupted.
4.  **Cutover:** The final migration is performed during a scheduled downtime window, ensuring a smooth transition to the new system.

Because of our prior experience with the source system, we can execute this migration efficiently and with low risk, ensuring that the City starts with PermitFlow with a complete and accurate historical record.

## REQ-17: Standard and custom reporting

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for standard and custom reporting. PermitFlow includes a powerful reporting engine designed for municipal planning departments.

**Standard Reports:**
We provide 30 standard reports out of the box. These cover common KPIs such as:
*   Number of applications by type/status.
*   Average review time by inspector or type.
*   Inspection pass/fail rates.
*   Revenue collected from fees.
*   Backlog analysis.

**Custom Reporting:**
In addition to standard reports, PermitFlow includes a **drag-and-drop report builder**. This allows City staff to create custom reports without needing to know SQL or coding. Users can:
*   Select data fields they want to include.
*   Apply filters (e.g., date range, permit type, zip code).
*   Choose grouping and sorting options.
*   Save the custom report for future use.

**Distribution:**
Reports can be viewed on-screen and **scheduled by email**. For example, the Planning Director can schedule the "Weekly Backlog Report" to be emailed to their inbox every Monday morning at 8:00 AM. This automation ensures that key stakeholders have timely access to data for decision-making.

This combination of ready-made insights and flexible customization meets the City’s reporting needs fully.

## REQ-18: Support during business hours, with 24/7 cover for critical incidents

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for support coverage. Our support model is tiered to match the severity of issues, ensuring efficient resource allocation and rapid response for critical problems.

**Business Hours Support:**
*   **Coverage:** 08:00 to 18:00, Monday through Friday (excluding public holidays).
*   **Channels:** Phone and Email.
*   **Scope:** General inquiries, how-to questions, non-critical bug reporting, and account management.
*   This covers the vast majority of support needs, ensuring staff can get help when they are working.

**24/7 Critical Incident Support:**
*   **Coverage:** 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including weekends and holidays.
*   **Channel:** Dedicated on-call phone line.
*   **Scope:** Severity-1 incidents only. A Severity-1 incident is defined as a **complete outage** of the PermitFlow platform, where the system is completely inaccessible to all users.
*   **Response Target:** We guarantee a **30-minute response time** for Severity-1 incidents. This means a senior engineer will acknowledge the incident and begin diagnostic work within 30 minutes of the City’s call.

This model ensures that the City receives immediate help during catastrophic failures while providing reliable support for day-to-day issues during working hours.

## REQ-19: On-premises deployment option

**Compliance: Not met**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software does **not** offer an on-premises deployment option for PermitFlow. We are strictly a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) provider.

**What is Missing:**
The ability to install and run PermitFlow on the City of Marlow Vale’s own servers or private cloud infrastructure.

**Why we do not offer this:**
1.  **Security and Maintenance:** SaaS allows us to centrally manage security patches, updates, and backups. This reduces the burden on the City’s IT staff and ensures a more secure and up-to-date system.
2.  **Scalability and Reliability:** Our cloud infrastructure is built for high availability and auto-scaling. Replicating this level of resilience on-premises would require significant hardware investment and specialized expertise from the City, which would increase costs and operational complexity for the City.

**Workaround/Mitigation:**
We strongly recommend that the City accept the SaaS model for the following reasons:
1.  **Data Sovereignty is Maintained:** As detailed in REQ-01, our hosting is within the country, ensuring data remains under local jurisdiction despite being hosted off-site.
2.  **Reduced IT Burden:** The City’s IT team does not need to manage patching, hardware refreshes, or backup infrastructure for PermitFlow. This frees up internal resources for other critical municipal IT projects.
3.  **Superior Security Posture:** SaaS allows for immediate deployment of security patches globally. In an on-premises model, there is often a lag between vulnerability discovery and patch application, increasing the risk of exploitation.
4.  **Cost Predictability:** The subscription model eliminates the unpredictable costs of hardware upgrades and emergency IT staffing associated with maintaining server infrastructure.

While we cannot meet the literal requirement for on-premises software, we believe the SaaS model offers superior security, reliability, and cost-effectiveness for the City of Marlow Vale. We are open to discussing this architecture decision with the IT Security Officer to address any specific concerns regarding control or data access.

## REQ-20: Training for staff

**Compliance: Full**

**Explanation:**
Tessellate Civic Software complies fully with the requirement for training staff. We provide a comprehensive training package designed to ensure successful user adoption and proficiency among all staff members, from plan reviewers to administrators.

**Training Methodology:**
1.  **Train-the-Trainer Sessions:** We conduct live, virtual, or on-site workshops (depending on City preference) for designated "Champions" within the Planning Department. These Champions become the internal experts, equipped with the knowledge to train their peers and answer day-to-day questions. This empowers the City to maintain independence from our support team for routine queries.
2.  **Role-Specific Content:** Training is tailored to specific roles. Inspectors receive training on the mobile app and field workflows; Reviewers focus on plan markup and decision logging; Administrators learn about role management, workflow configuration, and reporting.
3.  **Online Video Library:** We provide access to a permanent library of short, topic-specific video tutorials. These videos are searchable and can be accessed by staff at any time for refresher training or when onboarding new employees. This ensures that training materials are always available, reducing the need for repeated live sessions.

**Implementation Timeline:**
Training is delivered during the final phases of the 16-week implementation plan, ensuring that staff are trained on the configured system just before go-live. We also offer post-go-live follow-up sessions to address any questions that arise after the initial launch.

This blended approach of live training and self-service resources ensures high adoption rates and confident users.

# 5. Compliance Matrix

The following matrix summarizes the compliance status for each of the twenty requirements as detailed in Section 4.

| Requirement | Status | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| REQ-01 Cloud hosting within the country | Full | Hosted in two domestic data centers, 300 km apart. Data sovereignty guaranteed. |
| REQ-02 Availability of at least 99.9% per month | Full | Contractual 99.9% SLA. Measured 99.93% over last 12 months. Service credits apply. |
| REQ-03 Single sign-on with the city's identity provider | Full | Supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Integrates with standard municipal IdPs. |
| REQ-04 Multi-factor authentication for all users | Full | MFA built-in. Mandatory for admins; configurable for all users. Supports SSO inheritance. |
| REQ-05 Role-based access control, including city-defined custom roles | Partial | 12 predefined roles available today. Custom role creation is on roadmap for next year. |
| REQ-06 Audit trail of all actions on an application | Full | Logs views, changes, and decisions. Captures User ID, Timestamp, and Action. |
| REQ-07 Audit records retained for at least 7 years | Full | 10-year retention period (exceeds requirement). Exportable as CSV. |
| REQ-08 Public portal accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA | Full | Public applicant portal independently audited last year. Fully compliant with AA standards. |
| REQ-09 All user interfaces, including staff screens, accessible to WCAG 2.1 AA | Partial | Staff screens meet most AA criteria. 14 open issues identified; remediation committed within 6 months. |
| REQ-10 Online payment of permit fees | Full | Integration with City’s existing payment provider via standard API. Handles receipts and refunds. |
| REQ-11 Electronic plan review, including CAD drawings | Partial | Native markup for PDF/Image. No native DWG viewing. Workaround: Applicants convert DWG to PDF. |
| REQ-12 Mobile inspection app that works fully offline, including submitting results | Partial | Offline viewing supported. Submission requires online connectivity to ensure data integrity. |
| REQ-13 Encryption of data in transit and at rest | Full | TLS 1.2+ for transit; AES-256 for data at rest. |
| REQ-14 Annual independent security testing | Full | Annual penetration test by third party. Summary report shared with City under NDA. |
| REQ-15 Documented API for integration | Partial | Public REST API for Data (Apps, Inspections, Payments). No API for Workflow Configuration. |
| REQ-16 Migration of existing permit records | Full | Dedicated migration service. Prior experience migrating from City’s current system for 2 other authorities. |
| REQ-17 Standard and custom reporting | Full | 30 standard reports. Drag-and-drop custom builder. Scheduled email delivery supported. |
| REQ-18 Support during business hours, with 24/7 cover for critical incidents | Full | 08:00-18:00 Business Hours. 24/7 on-call for Sev-1 (complete outage) with 30-min response. |
| REQ-19 On-premises deployment option | Not met | SaaS only. No on-premises version. See Section 4 for justification and benefits of SaaS model. |
| REQ-20 Training for staff | Full | Train-the-Trainer sessions plus permanent online video library. Role-specific content. |

# 6. Implementation Plan

Tessellate proposes a structured 16-week implementation plan designed to minimize risk and ensure a smooth transition to PermitFlow. This plan leverages our prior experience with the City’s current system to accelerate data migration. The plan is divided into five phases.

### Phase 1: Discovery and Planning (Weeks 1–2)
**Objective:** Establish project governance, finalize configuration requirements, and prepare for data extraction.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Assign a dedicated Project Manager and Solution Architect.
*   Conduct kickoff meeting with City stakeholders (Planning, IT, Procurement).
*   Review and finalize the configuration workbook (workflows, roles, fee schedules).
*   Provide technical specifications for Single Sign-On (SSO) integration to the City’s IT team.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Designate a Project Sponsor and key functional leads (Admin, Reviewers, Inspectors).
*   Provide access to the current system’s database exports for schema analysis.
*   Confirm the configuration of the Identity Provider for SAML/OIDC testing.
*   Review and sign off on the proposed workflow diagrams.

### Phase 2: Configuration and Integration (Weeks 3–6)
**Objective:** Configure PermitFlow to match the City’s specific operational needs and establish secure connections.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Configure user roles, permissions, and workflow steps based on the Discovery phase.
*   Set up fee schedules and payment gateway integration with the City’s existing provider.
*   Develop custom reports required for initial go-live.
*   Execute SSO integration testing with the City’s IT team.
*   Begin data transformation scripts based on the legacy database exports.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Provide administrative access for Tessellate to configure the tenant.
*   Collaborate with the payment provider to authorize the integration.
*   Validate configured workflows and provide feedback on usability.
*   Review sample data from the migration transformation process for accuracy.

### Phase 3: Data Migration and Validation (Weeks 7–10)
**Objective:** Migrate historical data from the legacy system to PermitFlow and validate integrity.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Perform a full "dry run" data migration using anonymized test data.
*   Generate reconciliation reports comparing record counts and data checksums between the legacy system and PermitFlow.
*   Address any data quality issues identified during the dry run (e.g., invalid dates, missing fields).
*   Schedule the final cutover migration for the end of Week 10.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Validate the dry-run data. Functional leads must spot-check specific applications to ensure data looks correct.
*   Identify and correct source data errors in the legacy system that cannot be fixed by Tessellate.
*   Approve the final migration plan and cutover date.

### Phase 4: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Training (Weeks 11–14)
**Objective:** Ensure the system works as expected for end-users and train staff on new workflows.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Set up a UAT environment with production-like data (sanitized if necessary for privacy during testing, or full data if security permits).
*   Conduct Train-the-Trainer sessions for internal champions.
*   Provide access to online training videos and user guides.
*   Support the City’s UAT team and resolve any bugs or configuration issues found during testing.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Execute UAT scripts covering all key roles (Applicant, Reviewer, Inspector, Admin).
*   Log any defects or usability issues in the project management tool.
*   Champions deliver internal training to staff.
*   Sign off on UAT completion.

### Phase 5: Go-Live and Hypercare (Weeks 15–16)
**Objective:** Launch the system for production use and provide intensive support.

**Tessellate Responsibilities:**
*   Execute the final data cutover during a planned weekend downtime window.
*   Perform post-migration verification checks.
*   Monitor system performance closely during the first week.
*   Provide enhanced support (Hypercare) with priority response for any issues encountered by early adopters.

**City Responsibilities:**
*   Communicate go-live date and new procedures to applicants and the public.
*   Switch applicant portal traffic to PermitFlow.
*   Begin using PermitFlow for new applications.
*   Provide feedback to Tessellate on any immediate post-launch issues.

**Post-Go-Live:**
Following Week 16, the project transitions to standard support and ongoing account management. The remediation of the 14 accessibility issues in the staff UI (REQ-09) will continue in parallel and is committed to be completed within 6 months of contract signature.

# 7. Pricing

Tessellate Civic Software provides the following transparent pricing for the PermitFlow solution, hosted in two domestic data centers. All prices are exclusive of VAT where applicable. There are no hidden costs for hosting, updates, or standard support.

### Pricing Table

| Item | Description | Unit Price | Quantity | Total |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Annual Subscription** | Cloud hosting, software licenses, updates, and standard support (08:00–18:00). Includes 24/7 on-call for Sev-1 incidents. | €96,000 | 1 Year | €96,000 |
| **One-Off Implementation & Data Migration** | Project management, configuration, SSO integration, and migration of existing records from the current system. | €38,000 | 1 | €38,000 |
| **One-Off Training** | Train-the-Trainer sessions and provision of online video library. | €6,500 | 1 | €6,500 |

### Cost Summary

**First-Year Total Cost:**
The total cost for the first year of operation is **€140,500**.
*   This includes the first year of subscription (€96,000) plus the one-time implementation and training fees (€38,000 + €6,500).

**Five-Year Total Cost of Ownership:**
The total cost over five years is **€524,500**.
*   Calculation: (5 years × €96,000 annual subscription) + €38,000 implementation + €6,500 training.
*   Note: This price assumes no changes in the number of users or municipalities beyond the base scope. As a SaaS solution, there are no costs for hardware refreshes, server maintenance, or IT staff time dedicated to patching and backups, which are significant hidden costs in on-premises solutions.

### Payment Terms
*   **Year 1:** 50% of the one-off fees (€22,500) upon contract signature; the remaining 50% (€22,500) plus the first annual subscription (€96,000) upon Go-Live acceptance.
*   **Years 2–5:** Annual subscription fees billed annually in advance.

This pricing structure provides the City of Marlow Vale with a predictable operational expenditure, aligned with the benefits of a managed, secure, and continuously updated cloud service.
