# Hearthline T2 Smart Thermostat User Manual

Welcome to the Hearthline T2. This manual is designed to help you understand, set up, and get the most out of your new smart thermostat. The Hearthline T2 is built for homes with gas or oil boilers. It replaces your old wall dial or programmer. It gives you precise control over your home’s heating. It helps you save energy. It keeps your home comfortable.

This guide covers everything from the very first day of use to advanced settings. We have written this manual for homeowners, not engineers. The language is simple. The steps are clear. We explain technical terms when they first appear. If you need to find a specific setting, look for the bold menu path, such as **Menu > Heating > Schedule**. This tells you exactly where to go on the screen or in the app.

Please read the Safety Information first. Then, proceed through the chapters in order. Each chapter covers one main feature. By the end of this manual, you will feel confident using your Hearthline T2. You will be able to adjust settings with ease. You will understand how the system works. Let us begin.

## Safety Information

Your safety and the safety of others are our top priority. The Hearthline T2 is a safe device when used correctly. However, it involves electricity and heat. Please read these important warnings before you start using your thermostat. Keep this manual in a safe place. You may need it in the future. If you give this device to someone else, give them this manual too.

*   **Qualified Installation Only for the Receiver Box.** The receiver box connects directly to your boiler. It controls the power to the boiler. This involves mains electricity and potentially hazardous components. **The receiver box must only be opened or installed by a qualified installer.** Do not try to open the receiver box yourself. You could be seriously injured or damage your boiler. The wall unit, however, is designed for you to install. It uses batteries or low-voltage wiring. You can install the wall unit yourself. But the receiver must be handled by a professional.

*   **Avoid Direct Sunlight and Radiators.** The temperature sensor inside the wall unit measures the air temperature in your room. For accurate readings, the sensor must "see" the general room temperature. **Do not install the wall unit in direct sunlight.** The sun will heat the plastic casing. The sensor will read a false high temperature. Your heating will stay off when it should be on. **Do not install the wall unit above a radiator.** Heat rises. A radiator heats the air directly above it. If the thermostat is near a heat source, it will read a false high temperature. Install the wall unit on an internal wall. Choose a spot away from windows, doors, and heat sources. Ideally, place it at eye level. This is about 1.5 meters from the floor. This position gives the most accurate reading of the living space temperature.

*   **Keep Small Parts Away from Children.** The Hearthline T2 comes with small screws and wall plugs. These are small enough to be swallowed. They can cause choking hazards. **Keep all small parts away from children and pets.** When you install the wall unit, check the floor afterward. Pick up any dropped screws or plugs immediately. Dispose of packaging materials properly. Plastic bags and foam can also be dangerous for babies and toddlers. Store the extra parts in a high, locked cupboard if you have young children.

*   **Battery Safety.** The wall unit can run on two AA batteries. **Use only high-quality alkaline batteries.** Do not mix old and new batteries. Do not mix different brands of batteries. Do not use rechargeable batteries unless they are specifically rated for low-drift devices, as some rechargeables have lower voltage profiles that may cause reading errors. If you use the battery option, insert the batteries correctly. Match the plus (+) and minus (-) signs in the battery compartment. Incorrect insertion can damage the device. If the battery compartment is damaged or leaking fluid, stop using the wall unit immediately. Clean the contacts with a dry cloth. If corrosion is present, do not touch the fluid. The fluid is corrosive. It can burn your skin. Wear gloves. Dispose of the wall unit according to local electronic waste regulations. Do not throw batteries in the regular trash. Recycle them at a designated drop-off point.

*   **Wi-Fi Connectivity and Health.** The Hearthline T2 uses Wi-Fi to connect to your home network. Wi-Fi uses radio waves. These are non-ionizing radiation. They are generally considered safe for home use. However, if you have concerns about electromagnetic fields (EMF), you can minimize exposure. You can position the wall unit away from beds or prolonged seating areas. You can also disconnect the Wi-Fi in the app settings if you only want local control. Note that without Wi-Fi, you cannot use remote control features or receive weather updates. The device will still work as a local timer. The radio connection between the wall unit and the receiver is very low power. It is designed to be safe. It complies with all relevant safety standards. If you have a pacemaker or other implanted electronic device, consult your doctor. Some devices are sensitive to strong magnetic fields, though the T2’s fields are very weak.

*   **Water and Moisture.** The wall unit is designed for indoor use in dry rooms. **Do not install the wall unit in a bathroom, shower room, or any area with high humidity or water spray.** Water can short-circuit the electronics. It can cause the screen to malfunction. It can create a shock hazard. Do not clean the unit with a wet cloth. Use a slightly damp cloth only if necessary, and dry it immediately. Never submerge the wall unit in water. Do not splash water on it. If water does get inside, remove the batteries immediately. Let it dry completely for 48 hours before testing. If it does not work after drying, contact support. Do not attempt to repair it yourself.

*   **Choking Hazard for Batteries.** If the wall unit uses 24 V AC wiring, it may not have a battery compartment accessible from the front. If it does, and you have young children, be aware that button cells and AA batteries can be swallowed. Swallowing a battery is a medical emergency. It can cause severe internal burns within hours. If you suspect a child has swallowed a battery, seek emergency medical help immediately. Keep spare batteries in a container that cannot be opened by children.

## 1. Getting Started

Congratulations on your new Hearthline T2. This chapter explains how to get your system working. You will pair the wall unit with the receiver. You will connect the device to your home Wi-Fi. You will create an account in the Hearthline app. This setup takes about fifteen minutes. You will need your home Wi-Fi password. You will need your smartphone. You do not need tools for this part. The physical installation of the receiver is done by your installer. The physical installation of the wall unit is covered in a separate quick-start card. Here, we focus on the software setup.

### How to

Follow these steps to complete the initial setup. Make sure the receiver box is powered on and has been configured by your installer. Make sure the wall unit has batteries inserted or is wired for power. The screen on the wall unit should turn on.

1.  **Wake the Wall Unit.** Tap the center of the screen or rotate the ring slightly. The screen will light up. You will see a welcome message. It may ask you to select a language.
2.  **Pair the Wall Unit.** On the screen, look for the message "Pairing..." or go to **Menu > Settings > Pairing**. If the wall unit is new, it will automatically try to find the receiver. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the pairing process. The ring on the wall unit may vibrate slightly to confirm. Wait for the message "Pairing Successful."
3.  **Connect to Wi-Fi.** Go to **Menu > Network > Wi-Fi Setup**. The wall unit will scan for nearby Wi-Fi networks. Select your home network name from the list. Note: The T2 only supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If your router uses the same name for 5 GHz and 2.4 GHz, select the network. If it fails, you may need to create a separate 2.4 GHz name on your router. Type your Wi-Fi password using the on-screen keyboard. This is where you type carefully. Capital letters and numbers matter. Tap "Connect." The screen will show a progress bar. Wait for the message "Connected." The Wi-Fi icon will appear in the top corner of the screen.
4.  **Download the App.** Take your smartphone. Go to the Apple App Store or Google Play Store. Search for "Hearthline App." Download and install it. This app is free. It works on iOS and Android.
5.  **Create Your Account.** Open the Hearthline App. Tap "Create Account." Enter your name. Enter a valid email address. This email is used for login and password recovery. Create a strong password. Use a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols. Tap "Sign Up." You will receive an email with a confirmation link. Open your email on your phone. Click the link. Your account is now active.
6.  **Add Your Device.** In the app, tap the "+" icon or "Add Device." The app will search for devices connected to your Wi-Fi. Your Hearthline T2 should appear in the list. Tap on it. The app will ask for permission to use location services. You can allow this for now to enable Geofencing later. You can change this later if you prefer. Tap "Continue." The app will link the wall unit to your account. You will see a confirmation screen.
7.  **Verify Settings.** On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Settings > System Info**. Check that the Wi-Fi signal is strong. Check that the software version is 1.4. If it says "Update Required," tap "Update Now." The update will happen automatically. Do not turn off the power during an update.

### Settings

In the "Getting Started" phase, you can configure the basic display preferences. These settings control how the wall unit shows information. You can change them anytime. Go to **Menu > Settings > Preferences** on the wall unit, or **Settings > Preferences** in the app.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Language | English, French, German, Spanish | English |
| Temperature unit | °C or °F | °C |
| Time format | 12 h or 24 h | 24 h |

**Language** determines the text on the screen. If you choose French, all menus and messages will appear in French. **Temperature unit** changes the number on the screen. If you choose °C, it shows Celsius. If you choose °F, it shows Fahrenheit. Most European users use Celsius. **Time format** changes the clock. 24 h shows "17:30." 12 h shows "5:30 PM." Choose what is easiest for you to read.

### Troubleshooting

If you have trouble getting started, check these common issues.

*   **The wall unit cannot find the receiver.** Check that the receiver box has power. Look for an indicator light on the receiver. If there is no light, your installer needs to check the wiring. If there is light, ensure the wall unit is within 30 meters of the receiver. Thick brick walls or metal pipes can block the signal. Move the wall unit closer to the receiver temporarily to pair. Once paired, you can move it back. If it still fails, follow the on-screen prompts to restart the pairing process.
*   **Wi-Fi connection fails repeatedly.** Check that you are entering the correct password. Wi-Fi passwords are case-sensitive. Check that your router is broadcasting a 2.4 GHz signal. Many modern routers use "mesh" or "dual-band" systems. They combine 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz under one name. Sometimes smart devices get confused. Try turning off the 5 GHz band on your router temporarily. Or, if your router allows it, name the 2.4 GHz network differently, like "Home-Wi-Fi-2.4." Connect the T2 to that name. Also, check that your router firewall is not blocking new devices. Restart your router. Unplug it for 30 seconds. Plug it back in. Wait for it to fully start. Try connecting again.
*   **The app does not see the device.** Make sure your phone is on the same Wi-Fi network as the wall unit. If you are using mobile data, the app might not find the local device. Turn off mobile data. Connect your phone to Wi-Fi. Restart the app. If the device is still not found, remove it from the app if it was added previously. Add it again from scratch.
*   **The screen is blank.** If the wall unit is battery-powered, the batteries may be dead. Replace them with fresh AA batteries. If it is wired, check the 24 V AC supply. Ensure the wiring is secure. If the screen is cracked or physically damaged, contact support for replacement. If the screen shows a white light but no text, try removing the batteries. Wait one minute. Reinsert batteries. This clears any software glitches.

## 2. Manual Temperature Control

Sometimes you do not want to follow the schedule. You might be cold. You might be hot. You might be in a hurry to get the heat on. This is where manual control comes in. You can change the temperature at any time. You can override the schedule. This change can last for a short time. It can last until the next scheduled change. Or it can stay on permanently until you change it back.

There are two ways to control the temperature manually. You can use the physical ring on the wall unit. You can use the app on your phone. Both methods work instantly. The wall unit sends the command to the receiver. The receiver turns the boiler on or off. This chapter explains how to adjust the heat. It also explains how to set how long the change lasts.

### How to

Follow these steps to change the temperature manually.

1.  **Adjust via the Wall Unit.** Stand in front of the wall unit. Wake the screen by tapping it. Look at the large number in the center. This is the current target temperature. Rotate the ring clockwise to increase the temperature. Rotate counter-clockwise to decrease it. The number on the screen will change. It changes in steps of 0.5 °C. Stop rotating when you reach the number you want. The wall unit will beep softly. The ring will vibrate slightly to confirm. The change is now active.
2.  **Set the Hold Duration on the Wall Unit.** After changing the temperature, a small menu may appear at the bottom of the screen. It asks, "Hold for?" You can tap the screen to select options. Options include "Next Schedule Change," "1 Hour," "2 Hours," etc., up to "Permanent." If you do not select an option, it defaults to "Next Schedule Change."
3.  **Adjust via the App.** Open the Hearthline App. Tap on your Hearthline T2 device. You will see the current room temperature and the target temperature. You can drag a slider up or down. Or you can tap the plus (+) and minus (-) buttons. Each tap changes the temperature by 0.5 °C. The app sends the command to the device immediately. You will see a loading icon. Then the temperature on the screen will update.
4.  **Set the Hold Duration in the App.** When you change the temperature in the app, a popup will ask how long to hold this temperature. Select "Until next change" from the dropdown. Or select a specific duration like "2 hours." Or select "Permanent." If you select "Permanent," the schedule will stop working. The house will stay at this new temperature until you manually change it again. To clear a permanent hold, you must change the temperature again and select the option to return to schedule mode.
5.  **View Current Status.** On the main screen of the wall unit, you will see an icon if a manual hold is active. It might say "Manual" or "Hold." In the app, the schedule timeline will be grayed out during a hold. This tells you that the automated plan is paused.

### Settings

These settings control the limits and defaults for manual changes. You can find these in **Menu > Heating > Limits** or in the app under **Settings > Manual Control**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Target temperature | 5–30 °C in 0.5 °C steps | 20 °C |
| Hold duration | Until next schedule change, 1–12 hours, or permanent | Until next schedule change |

**Target temperature** defines the lowest and highest temperature you can manually select. The minimum is 5 °C. The maximum is 30 °C. You cannot set it below 5 °C because that is too cold for the system’s minimum logic. You cannot set it above 30 °C to prevent overheating. The **steps** mean you can choose 20.0, 20.5, 21.0, and so on. You cannot choose 20.3 °C. The **default** is 20 °C. This is the temperature used if no other setting applies. It is the starting point for many features.

**Hold duration** controls how long your manual change stays active. The default is "Until next schedule change." This is the most common use. You are cold now, but you want the normal schedule to resume in a few hours. If you choose a specific number of hours, like "3," the hold will end exactly three hours from now. Even if the schedule changes before then, the hold takes priority until the time expires. If you choose "Permanent," the hold never ends automatically. You must go back and cancel it. This is useful if you are going on a trip and want the heat fixed at a specific level, though Holiday Mode is better for trips.

### Troubleshooting

Check these issues if manual control does not seem to work.

*   **Changing the temperature does nothing.** Check if the Child Lock is on. If the lock is on, the ring and screen will not respond to changes. Unlock it using the PIN. Check if the boiler has faulted. Look for an error code on the wall unit. If there is an error, manual control will not start the boiler until the error is cleared. Check the Wi-Fi connection. If the wall unit is offline, it may not accept commands from the app. It should still accept commands from the ring. If the ring does not change the temperature, the internal motor or sensor may be faulty. Contact support.
*   **The temperature jumps back after a few seconds.** This is normal if the hold duration is short. For example, if you set a 1-hour hold at 2 PM, it will revert at 3 PM. Check your hold duration settings. Another possibility is that a Geofence rule is overriding your manual control. If everyone is away, Geofencing might force the Eco temperature. Check if your Geofence radius is too small. Try moving your phone further away to test. Ensure your phone’s location services are accurate.
*   **The temperature does not match the boiler output.** The thermostat measures the air temperature in the room. It does not measure the water temperature in the boiler. If the room is warm, the thermostat may think it has reached the target. The boiler might still be running to push heat into the radiators. This is a delay known as thermal lag. To help, ensure the room air can reach the sensor. Do not block the wall unit with furniture. If the mismatch is extreme, the sensor may be dirty or placed in a draft. Clean the unit. Move it away from vents. If the problem persists, the calibration may be off. Contact support for calibration advice.
*   **Cannot select temperatures above 20 °C.** You may have hit a user-defined limit. Check the "Max Temperature" setting in your advanced settings. Some users set this to save energy. If the max is set to 20, you cannot go higher. Change the max temperature in the settings. Or, check if you are in a specific mode like "Eco Mode." In Eco Mode, the maximum temperature is capped. Exit Eco Mode to adjust the temperature higher.

## 3. Weekly Schedule

The Weekly Schedule is the core feature of your Hearthline T2. It automates your heating. It turns the heat on when you need it. It turns the heat off when you do not. This saves energy. It saves money. It ensures comfort. You set it once. It repeats every week. You can have different schedules for weekdays and weekends. You can even have different schedules for each day of the week.

A schedule consists of "periods." A period is a block of time. Each period has a start time and a target temperature. For example, a period might start at 06:30 with a target of 20 °C. It ends when the next period starts. You can have up to six periods per day. This allows for a very detailed plan. For example, you can have a night period, a morning wake-up period, a day work period, an evening relax period, and a late-night sleep period.

The app makes it easy to copy schedules. You do not need to set up Monday and Tuesday separately if they are the same. You can create Monday. Then copy Monday’s schedule to Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. This saves time.

### How to

Follow these steps to set up your weekly schedule. You can do this on the wall unit, but the app is much easier for detailed schedules.

1.  **Open the Schedule Editor in the App.** Open the Hearthline App. Tap your device. Tap **Schedule** in the menu bar. You will see a seven-day view. Each day shows a bar graph. The height of the bar shows the target temperature over time.
2.  **Set the Number of Periods.** Tap on the day you want to edit, for example, "Monday." A timeline will appear. By default, there are four periods. You can add more. Tap the "+" button to add a period. You can remove a period by tapping the "-" button. The maximum is six periods. The minimum is one.
3.  **Define the Period Times.** Tap on the start time of the first period. An on-screen clock will appear. Set the time. For example, set the first period to start at 06:30. Tap "Save." The end time of this period is automatically the start time of the next period. If it is the last period of the day, it ends at 23:59 and loops to the start of the next day. You can adjust the start times of each period by tapping the divider lines between periods. Drag the line left or right to change the start time of the following period.
4.  **Set the Target Temperature for Each Period.** Tap on the colored bar of a period. A temperature slider will appear. Slide it to the desired temperature. For example, set the morning period to 21 °C. The bar height will change to reflect the temperature. Do this for each period. A typical day might look like this: 06:30 (20 °C), 08:30 (17 °C), 17:00 (21 °C), 22:30 (16 °C).
5.  **Review the Visual Graph.** The graph shows when the heat is high and when it is low. Look for gaps. Ensure you have not accidentally set a high temperature during work hours if you are never home. Ensure the night temperature is low enough to save energy but high enough for comfort.
6.  **Copy the Day.** Once Monday is perfect, tap "Copy." You will see options for other days. Tap Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. Tap "Confirm." All these days now have the exact same schedule as Monday. This ensures consistency.
7.  **Set the Weekend.** Tap on Saturday. Adjust the periods to match your weekend routine. You might sleep in later. You might be home all day. Adjust the times and temperatures accordingly. You can copy Saturday to Sunday if your weekend is the same.
8.  **Save and Apply.** Tap "Done" or "Save." The schedule is now active. The wall unit will sync this data. The heating will follow this plan starting immediately.

### Settings

These settings are global. They affect how the schedule functions. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule > Advanced** or in the app under **Settings > Schedule**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Periods per day | 1–6 | 4 |
| Copy day | Any day to any other days | N/A |
| Default periods | 06:30 20 °C, 08:30 17 °C, 17:00 21 °C, 22:30 16 °C | 06:30 20 °C, 08:30 17 °C, 17:00 21 °C, 22:30 16 °C |

**Periods per day** limits how many temperature blocks you can have in a 24-hour day. The default is 4. This is sufficient for most households. If you have a shift work pattern, you might need 5 or 6. You cannot have more than 6. If you want fewer, you can delete periods. This makes the schedule simpler to read.

**Copy day** is not a stored value but an action. However, it is listed here as a setting option in the sense of its availability. It allows you to duplicate the configuration of one day to one or more other days. This is crucial for maintaining consistency without re-entering data. If you change one day, remember that copied days do not auto-update. You must copy again.

**Default periods** refers to the initial configuration when you first create a schedule or if you reset to factory defaults. The system provides a sensible starting point. It assumes a standard work day. It warms up before you wake up. It cools down when you leave for work. It warms up when you return. It cools down for sleep. You should customize these values to fit your life. Do not rely on the defaults if your routine is different.

### Troubleshooting

*   **The schedule does not seem to change the temperature.** Check the current mode. Is the system in "Manual Hold"? A manual hold overrides the schedule. Check the app. Is there an "Away" mode active? Geofencing or Holiday Mode overrides the schedule. Check the Wi-Fi. If the wall unit is offline, it may be running on a cached schedule. Force a sync in the app. Go to **Settings > Sync**.
*   **The temperature is too cold in the morning.** The schedule might start too late. If you wake up at 7:00 AM, and the first period starts at 07:00, the house will be cold. The boiler takes time to heat the radiators. This is called "Pre-heating." The T2 tries to compensate, but it may not be enough. Move the start time earlier. For example, start the warm-up at 05:30 for a 07:00 wake-up. Or, increase the temperature for the first period. Ensure the boiler is functioning correctly. Check for air in the radiators. Bleed them if necessary.
*   **The temperature is too hot during the day.** You may have a period set to a high temperature during work hours. Check the schedule graph. Ensure the mid-day temperature is set to the Eco temperature or a low comfort level. If you use Open Window Detection, check if that is triggering. If a window is open, the system might ignore the schedule to save energy. Close all windows. Wait for the sensor to stabilize.
*   **I cannot add a period.** You have reached the limit of 6 periods per day. Delete one period to add a new one. You cannot have overlapping periods. The end time of one period must be the start time of the next. If you try to drag a line past another line, the app will prevent it. Check that the times are in chronological order. You cannot have a period start at 10:00 AM and the next start at 08:00 AM. The day must flow from 00:00 to 23:59.
*   **Copied days look different.** Did you change the source day after copying? Copies are static snapshots. They do not update automatically. To fix this, copy the source day again to the target days. Alternatively, edit each day manually. This is tedious. It is better to plan changes in the source day and then re-copy.

## 4. Away Mode and Geofencing

Away Mode is a smart feature. It uses your smartphone’s location. It knows when you leave home. It knows when you return. This feature is called Geofencing. A "geofence" is a virtual boundary. You set it around your home. It looks like a circle on a map. When all registered users leave this circle, the Hearthline T2 switches to Away Mode. In Away Mode, the heating drops to the Eco temperature. This saves energy while you are gone.

When the first user re-enters the circle, the system switches back to the normal schedule. It can also "pre-heat." Pre-heating means turning the heating on *before* you arrive. This ensures the house is warm when you walk through the door. Without pre-heating, the schedule would wait until you entered the circle. It might take 30 minutes to warm up. With pre-heating, the system calculates the distance and traffic. It starts heating early.

This feature requires your phone’s location services to be enabled. It requires the Hearthline App to have permission to access location. It requires at least one user to be paired with the home.

### How to

Set up Geofencing to automate your heating.

1.  **Enable Location Services.** On your iPhone, go to Settings > Privacy > Location Services > Hearthline. Select "Always." This is important. If you select "While Using," the app will not know when you leave if it is closed in the background. On Android, go to Settings > Apps > Hearthline > Permissions > Location. Select "Allow all the time." Allow this for every household member who needs to trigger the Away mode.
2.  **Set Up Your Location.** Open the Hearthline App. Go to **Settings > Geofencing**. Tap "Add Location." You will see a map. Tap the map where your home is. Or use "My Current Location" if you are standing in your house. Name the location "Home." Tap Save.
3.  **Adjust the Geofence Radius.** You will see a circle on the map. You can resize it by pinching the screen or dragging the edge. The radius determines how far away you must be before Away Mode triggers. A larger radius triggers Away Mode sooner. A smaller radius triggers it later. Start with the default. You can adjust it later based on how it feels.
4.  **Enable Return Pre-heat.** In the same menu, find "Return Pre-heat." Ensure the toggle is set to "On." This tells the system to calculate when to start heating before you arrive. If you have a large house with high thermal mass, this is very useful. If you have a small, well-insulated home, you might not need it. But it is generally recommended to keep it on.
5.  **Add More Users.** If you live with others, invite them. Each user must follow step 1 and enable location. Once they accept the invite in the app, their phones become part of the Geofence logic. Away Mode only triggers when *all* paired users have left the zone. If you leave but your spouse is still home, the heating stays on. This is a safety feature. It ensures the home is warm for those who are still there.
6.  **Test Away Mode.** Wait for a time when everyone leaves the house. Check the app. The status should change to "Away." The target temperature should drop to the Eco temperature. Check the wall unit screen. It should show an "Away" icon. When you return, wait for the status to change back to "Normal" or the schedule. Feel the temperature rise.

### Settings

Configure the sensitivity of the Geofencing feature. Go to **Settings > Geofencing** in the app.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Geofence radius | 200–2,000 m | 500 m |
| Return pre-heat | On/Off | On |

**Geofence radius** defines the size of the virtual circle. The minimum is 200 meters. The maximum is 2,000 meters. The default is 500 meters. This is about a 5-minute drive or a 15-minute walk from your door. If the radius is too small, Away Mode might trigger only when you are already far away. This wastes energy. If the radius is too large, Away Mode might trigger when you are still at the end of the driveway. This might interrupt your pre-heat if you are coming back quickly. 500 meters is a good balance for suburban areas. In rural areas with long driveways, you might increase it to 1,000 meters. In cities with GPS drift, you might decrease it to 300 meters.

**Return pre-heat** is a binary switch. It is either On or Off. When **On**, the algorithm estimates your arrival time based on your movement speed. It starts the heating process to reach the target temperature by the time you enter the geofence. This uses complex logic involving weather and house insulation estimates. When **Off**, the system switches back to the normal schedule instantly when you re-enter the zone. The house will start warming up then. It will be cold when you walk in. For most users, On is the better choice for comfort.

### Troubleshooting

*   **Away Mode does not trigger.** Check Location Services. Ensure the app has "Always" permission. Check your phone’s battery saver mode. Battery saver often kills background location tracking. Disable battery saver for the Hearthline App specifically. Check if all users have left. If one user’s phone is still in the zone (or if their phone has a stale location cache), the mode will not trigger. Try forcing a location update in the app. Check the Wi-Fi. Geofencing data must sync to the device. If offline, the device may not receive the command immediately.
*   **Away Mode triggers too often.** The radius might be too large. You might be leaving the zone for a short trip to the shops. The system thinks you are gone for hours. Reduce the radius to 200–300 meters. Check if your phone is losing GPS signal. If your phone jumps location randomly, it might exit the zone erroneously. Update your phone’s GPS data. Ensure you are outdoors when the status changes.
*   **Pre-heat does not warm the house.** Check if the boiler is working. If the boiler has a fault, it will not heat. Check the schedule. If the normal schedule has a very low temperature, pre-heat might conflict with it. Ensure the pre-heat logic is not capped by the Eco temperature. Check your home’s insulation. In very poorly insulated homes, pre-heat might not be enough. You might need to manually raise the schedule temperature in the evening. Check the app for logs. Go to **Settings > Activity Log**. Look for "Pre-heat started." If it is not there, the app is not calculating correctly. Try toggling Pre-heat off and on again.
*   **Multiple users cause confusion.** Remember, Away Mode requires *all* users to be away. If you set up 3 users, but only 2 phones are present, the heating will stay on. Ensure everyone has installed the app and enabled location. If someone does not want to be tracked, do not add them to the Geofence user list. Add them as a "Guest" with no Geofence permissions. They can still control the heat manually, but their presence will not stop Away Mode.

## 5. Eco Temperature

Eco Temperature is your backup plan. It is the temperature the heating system aims for when it is "off" or in low-energy modes. It is not just for when you are away. It is also used during long gaps in the schedule. It is used in Holiday Mode. It is the baseline for energy saving.

Think of Eco Temperature as your "security minimum." It is warm enough to keep pipes from freezing (though Frost Protection is lower). It is warm enough to be comfortable if you come home quickly. It is cool enough to save significant energy. By setting a specific Eco Temperature, you ensure consistency. You do not have to guess what "low" means.

You can adjust this temperature to suit your needs. If you are sensitive to cold, you might set it to 18 °C. If you are away for weeks, you might set it to 10 °C. The default is 16 °C. This is a widely accepted standard for energy savings in European climates.

### How to

Set your Eco Temperature.

1.  **Access Settings.** Go to **Menu > Settings > Temperature** on the wall unit. Or go to **Settings > Temperature** in the app.
2.  **Find Eco Temperature.** Scroll down until you see "Eco Temperature" or "Away Temperature."
3. **Adjust the Value.** Tap the setting. A number wheel or slider will appear. Turn the ring on the wall unit or drag the slider in the app to change the value. The range is between 10 °C and 20 °C. The system will show you the current selection. For example, ifyou are energy-conscious, you might choose 12 °C. If you want to return to a warmer home, choose 18 °C. Tap "Save" or press the center of the ring to confirm.

### Settings

These settings define the floor for your energy-saving modes. You can find this in **Menu > Settings > Temperature > Eco** or **Settings > Temperature** in the app.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Eco temperature | 10–20 °C | 16 °C |

**Eco temperature** is the single most important setting for energy saving during absences. The minimum is 10 °C. This is the lowest you can go. It is close to the frost protection limit. It saves the maximum amount of energy. The maximum is 20 °C. This is the same as your typical comfort target. If you set it to 20 °C, you gain no energy savings when away. The default is 16 °C. This strikes a balance. It keeps the house from feeling "dead" cold. It protects plumbing. It uses significantly less fuel than heating to 21 °C.

### Troubleshooting

*   **The house feels too cold when I return.** Your Eco temperature may be set too low. If you return after a long day, the house might be at 12 °C. This feels freezing. Try raising the Eco temperature to 16 or 18 °C. Also, check your Return Pre-heat settings. If pre-heat is off, the house will start heating from the Eco temperature when you arrive. It will take time to warm up. Enabling pre-heat helps compensate for a low Eco setting.
*   **Energy usage is higher than expected.** Check if the Eco temperature is set too high. If you are set to 20 °C while away, you are heating the house as much as when you are home. Lower the Eco temperature to 16 °C or lower. Also, check for leaks in your home. Drafts from windows or doors can make the sensor read a low temperature. The boiler will then run longer to reach the Eco target. Seal drafts to improve efficiency.
*   **The temperature does not drop to Eco mode.** Check if a Manual Hold is active. A manual hold keeps the target temperature at the manual level, ignoring the Eco rule. Check if a specific schedule period is overriding the Away mode. Ensure that Geofencing is working. If your phone is still within the geofence radius, the system thinks you are home. Check the app status. It should say "Away." If it says "Home," the Eco temperature will not apply.
*   **Pipes are freezing.** This is rare if your Eco temperature is above 10 °C. However, if you set Eco to 10 °C and the weather is extreme, it might not be enough for exposed pipes in the loft or garage. The Frost Protection feature (Chapter 9) is the safety net for this. Ensure Frost Protection is active. It will turn on the heating if the temperature drops below the frost threshold, regardless of the Eco setting. Do not rely on Eco temperature for freezing protection alone.

## 6. Boost

Boost is for emergencies. You are cold *right now*. You are coming home *now*. You do not want to wait for the schedule or pre-heat calculation. You want heat immediately. Boost forces the boiler to run at full power for a set time. It ignores the usual throttling or modulation that saves energy. It pushes the system hard to raise the room temperature quickly.

When you activate Boost, the target temperature temporarily rises. By default, it rises by 2 °C above your current target. The boiler stays on until this new target is reached or the timer ends. This uses more energy. It is not meant for everyday use. Use it sparingly. Use it when comfort is critical and speed is needed.

### How to

Activate Boost mode.

1.  **Activate via the Wall Unit.** On the wall unit screen, swipe down from the top or tap the main area to reveal quick actions. Look for the "Boost" icon. It usually looks like a flame or a lightning bolt. Tap it. A timer countdown will appear. The default is 60 minutes. You can adjust this before starting if needed. The screen will change to show "Boost Active." The ring may vibrate to confirm activation.
2.  **Activate via the App.** Open the Hearthline App. Tap your device. On the main control screen, look for the "Boost" button. It is often near the temperature dial. Tap "Start Boost." A menu will ask how long you want the boost to last. Select your desired duration. Tap "Confirm." The app will show a boost indicator. The wall unit will also update to show the boost status.
3.  **Adjust Boost Duration.** Before starting, you can change how long the boost lasts. Go to **Menu > Heating > Boost** on the wall unit or **Settings > Boost** in the app. Select 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes. 30 minutes is for a quick warm-up. 120 minutes is for a cold room that needs significant warming. Choose the duration that fits your needs.
4.  **Monitor the Boost.** During boost, the current temperature will rise rapidly. Watch the number on the screen. When the timer reaches zero, the boost ends. The target temperature returns to whatever the schedule says. If you are still cold, you may need to run Boost again. Or adjust your normal schedule target higher.

### Settings

These settings control the intensity and length of the boost feature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Boost > Options** or **Settings > Boost**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Boost duration | 30, 60, 90 or 120 minutes | 60 minutes |
| Boost temperature | Default target + 2 °C | Default target + 2 °C |

**Boost duration** determines how long the high-power mode lasts. You can choose 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes. The default is 60 minutes. This is an hour. It is enough to make a noticeable difference in a standard room. If your boiler takes a long time to heat water, 60 minutes might not reach the target. You may need 90 or 120 minutes. If you have a small bathroom, 30 minutes might be sufficient. Avoid using the maximum duration unnecessarily. It wastes energy.

**Boost temperature** is calculated automatically. It is your current target temperature plus 2 °C. This is a fixed rule in firmware 1.4. You cannot change this offset to +5 °C or +10 °C. This limitation is for safety and efficiency. Increasing the target by 2 °C is usually enough to push the boiler to full output. The boiler will run at maximum capacity until this higher target is met. Once the boost time ends, the target reverts.

### Troubleshooting

*   **The room does not get hotter.** Check if the boiler is actually running. Look for the "Heating On" icon on the wall unit. If the boiler is off, the boost is not working. Check for boiler faults. If the boiler has a fault, it cannot provide heat. Check your water pressure. If the system pressure is low, the boiler may lock out. Consult your boiler manual. Check your home insulation. If the room is very drafty, the heat loss may match the heat gain. Boost cannot overcome massive heat loss. Close windows and doors during boost.
*   **The boost turns off too soon.** Did you set the duration to 30 minutes? Check your Boost Duration setting. If you want it to last longer, select 60 or 90 minutes. Also, check if the target temperature was reached before the timer ended. Boost ends early if the target is reached. This is normal. It stops to save energy. If the target is not reached but it stopped, check for manual overrides. Did someone change the temperature manually during the boost? That might cancel the boost logic.
*   **The target temperature is not higher.** The boost adds 2 °C to the *current* target. If your current target is already high, say 25 °C, boost will try to reach 27 °C. If your target is at the maximum 30 °C, boost cannot increase it further. Check your base temperature. Ensure it is not already at the upper limit. If you are trying to boost from 20 °C, the system should aim for 22 °C. Verify this on the screen. If the screen still shows 20 °C, refresh the display. Tap the screen.
*   **Boost uses too much electricity/gas.** Boost is high-intensity. It is normal for it to use more energy. Do not use Boost as your primary heating method. Use it for exceptions. If you find yourself using Boost every day, your schedule is wrong. Adjust your schedule to heat earlier or higher. Reduce reliance on Boost. You can also lower the Eco temperature so the starting point for the day is lower, allowing the schedule to do more of the work efficiently.

## 7. Hot Water Control

Some homes have a separate hot-water cylinder. This is a tank that stores hot water for showers and washing. The Hearthline T2 can control this if your system is wired correctly. This is common in systems with a two-port valve. The thermostat can tell the valve to open and fill the cylinder.

Hot water heating is separate from central heating. You can heat water when you do not want to heat the rooms. This is useful at night. Electricity or gas might be cheaper at night. Or you might want hot water ready in the morning. You do not want the radiators to be hot in the summer, but you still need hot water. The T2 handles this separation.

Note: This feature only works if your installer connected the "CH" (Central Heating) and "HW" (Hot Water) wires correctly to the receiver. If you do not see these options, your installer may have configured it for central heating only.

### How to

Set up your hot water schedule.

1.  **Access Hot Water Settings.** In the app, go to **Settings > Hot Water**. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Hot Water**. Ensure this option exists. If it is grayed out, your installer did not enable it. Contact them.
2.  **Enable Hot Water Control.** If there is a toggle for "Enable Hot Water," set it to On. This allows the system to manage the hot water valve independently of the room heating.
3.  **Create a Hot Water Schedule.** Tap **Schedule > Hot Water**. You can set up to three periods per day. This is simpler than the heating schedule. For example, set Period 1 to start at 05:00 and end at 06:30. Set the target to "Hot" or "On." Period 2 might be at midday if you have guests. Period 3 might be in the evening.
4.  **Set Hot Water Target.** For each period, select whether the hot water should be "On" (heating) or "Off" (off). Some advanced settings might allow a target temperature, but generally, the T2 uses on/off control for the cylinder. It fills the tank until the thermostat in the tank calls for heat.
5.  **Use Hot Water Boost.** If you need hot water immediately and the schedule does not cover it, use Boost. On the app main screen, tap the Hot Water tab. Tap "Boost." Select 30 or 60 minutes. This forces the boiler to prioritize hot water. The cylinder will heat up rapidly. After the time ends, it returns to the schedule.

### Settings

These settings apply only to homes with hot water cylinders. Go to **Settings > Hot Water**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hot water schedule | Up to 3 periods per day | N/A |
| Hot water boost | 30 or 60 minutes | 60 minutes |

**Hot water schedule** allows up to three distinct time slots. You cannot have more. This is because hot water tanks are large. They take time to fill. Three periods usually cover: early morning fill, daytime top-up (optional), and evening fill. Keep the schedule simple. Overlapping periods are not allowed. The times must be in order.

**Hot Water boost** duration is limited to 30 or 60 minutes. The default is 60 minutes. 30 minutes is good for a quick shower top-up. 60 minutes is for a full tank recovery. If you run out of hot water, start a 60-minute boost. It is unlikely that 30 minutes will heat a full cold tank. Be patient. The boiler needs to run for the full duration if the tank is cold.

### Troubleshooting

*   **No hot water is being produced.** Check if the Hot Water Schedule is set to "On" for the current time. Check if the cylinder thermostat is set to a temperature higher than the water temperature. If the water in the tank is already hot, the boiler will not fire. Check the system pressure. Low pressure can prevent the valve from operating. Check for airlocks in the system. Bleed the radiators or the pump if necessary. Ensure the receiver box has power.
*   **The hot water does not stop heating.** The cylinder thermostat might be faulty. It is stuck in the "closed" position, telling the boiler to heat forever. The T2 is doing its job, but the boiler thinks it needs more heat. You may need a plumber to replace the cylinder thermostat. Alternatively, the wiring might be reversed. The "CH" and "HW" terminals might be swapped at the boiler. Contact your installer if the hot water heats when you want central heating.
*   **Boost does not change the status.** Ensure you are boosting Hot Water, not Heating. Check the tab you are on in the app. Look for the Hot Water icon (usually a tap or water drop). If you are on the Heating tab, the boost applies to the rooms. Check if the hot water schedule is currently in a long "Off" period. Boost overrides the schedule for the set duration. If the boost icon is not available, the feature might be disabled in settings. Enable it.
*   **Hot water is lukewarm.** The cylinder might not be fully heating. Check if the insulation on the cylinder is intact. Heat escapes if the insulation is damaged. Check if the immersion heater (if you have one) is on. It might conflict with the boiler heating. Turn off the immersion heater to let the boiler handle it. Check the flow rate. If the diverter valve is sticking, it might mix hot and cold water incorrectly.

## 8. Holiday Mode

Holiday Mode is for when you are gone for days or weeks. It is more powerful than Away Mode. Away Mode is for short trips. Holiday Mode sets a specific temperature for a specific date range. It ignores your weekly schedule. It ensures you come home to a pre-warmed house on the day you return.

You set a start date and an end date. During this time, the heating maintains the Holiday Temperature. This temperature is usually lower than the Eco temperature. It is set to 12 °C by default. This keeps the pipes safe and the house from getting too damp, but it uses minimal energy.

You can also set a "Return Time." The system will start heating *before* your return date to reach comfort levels by the time you arrive. This is useful if you are on a long flight or drive. You do not want to come home to a freezing house and wait hours for it to warm up.

### How to

Set up Holiday Mode for your upcoming trip.

1.  **Access Holiday Mode.** In the app, go to **Settings > Holiday Mode**. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday**.
2.  **Set Start and End Dates.** Tap "Start Date." Use the calendar picker to select the day you leave. Tap "End Date." Select the day you return. For example, if you leave on Monday and return on Sunday, set those dates. The system will stay in Holiday Mode from the start of the start day until the end of the end day.
3.  **Set the Holiday Temperature.** Tap the temperature setting. Adjust it to your preference. The default is 12 °C. You can set it between 5 °C and 15 °C. 12 °C is a good standard. If you are worried about frozen pipes in a very cold winter, keep it at 12 °C. If you are in a mild climate, you might drop it to 8 °C to save more money.
4.  **Activate Holiday Mode.** Tap "Start" or "Activate." The wall unit screen will change. It will show a palm tree or suitcase icon. The target temperature will drop to the Holiday setting immediately. The weekly schedule is now suspended.

### Settings

Configure the parameters for your holiday. Go to **Settings > Holiday**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Start and end dates | Calendar dates | N/A |
| Holiday temperature | 5–15 °C | 12 °C |

**Start and end dates** define the active period. The system checks the date and time. Once the end date passes, the system automatically reverts to the normal Weekly Schedule. You do not need to remember to turn it off. This is a key feature. It prevents you from coming home to an unexpectedly cold or hot house due to forgetting to reset. Ensure the dates are correct. Time zones matter if you travel across time zones, but the T2 uses your local home time zone.

**Holiday temperature** is the target during the break. The range is 5–15 °C. The default is 12 °C. The minimum of 5 °C is close to the frost limit. It provides maximum savings. The maximum of 15 °C is cooler than a normal room. You can go up to 15 °C if you want to keep the house feeling lived-in, perhaps to deter burglars or reduce condensation. But 12 °C is the sweet spot for most users.

### Troubleshooting

*   **The heating turned on before the start date.** Check if you have two overlapping holiday periods. Delete and recreate the holiday period cleanly. Ensure the start date is in the future.
*   **The house is freezing during the holiday.** Check the Holiday Temperature setting. If it is set to 5 °C, that is very cold. Check if the Frost Protection feature is active. Frost Protection should override the Holiday Temperature if the actual temperature drops below the frost limit (default 7 °C). If the house is below 7 °C and the boiler is not running, there is a fault in the Frost Protection logic or the boiler. This is serious. Contact support immediately. Check for power cuts at home. If the power was out, the date/time might be wrong. Reset the clock.
*   **The house is too hot when I return.** The Holiday Temperature may have been set too high (15 °C). Or the normal schedule starts immediately upon return and is set to a high temperature. Check the schedule for your return day. Ensure it aligns with your arrival time.
*   **Holiday Mode does not deactivate.** The end date may not have passed yet. Check the current date and time on the device. If the clock is wrong, the system might think it is still on holiday. Set the time manually in **Settings > Time**. If the date is correct but the mode persists, restart the wall unit. Remove batteries for 30 seconds. Reinsert. Check the app. It might be a cache issue. Pull down to refresh.

## 9. Frost Protection

Frost Protection is a critical safety feature. It is always active. It cannot be turned off. This is by design. It protects your pipes from bursting. If your home gets very cold, the T2 will turn on the heating. This happens even if your schedule says "Off." Even if you are in Holiday Mode. Even if you are in Away Mode.

The system monitors the room temperature. If it falls below the "Frost Temperature," the boiler fires. It heats the room until the temperature rises above the frost threshold by a small margin. This ensures that the water in your pipes does not freeze. Frozen water expands. It bursts pipes. It causes massive water damage. Frost Protection prevents this.

The default frost temperature is 7 °C. You can adjust this. You should not set it too high. That wastes energy. You should not set it too low. That risks freezing. 7 °C is a safe margin below the freezing point of water (0 °C), accounting for heat loss and sensor delays.

### How to

Verify your Frost Protection settings.

1.  **Access Frost Settings.** Go to **Menu > Settings > Safety > Frost Protection** on the wall unit. Or go to **Settings > Safety** in the app.
2.  **Check the Status.** You will see that Frost Protection is "Enabled." Note that the toggle is grayed out or locked. You cannot turn it off. This is to ensure you never accidentally disable it.
3.  **Adjust the Temperature.** Tap the "Frost Temperature" value. Use the ring or slider to change it. The range is 5–12 °C. The default is 7 °C. If you have very poorly insulated pipes, you might raise it to 8 or 9 °C. If you have a very efficient system, you might try 6 °C, but be cautious. Tap Save.
4.  **Monitor during Winter.** In extreme cold, keep an eye on the room temperature. If you see the heating turning on unexpectedly when the schedule says it should be off, it is likely Frost Protection. Check the app activity log. It will say "Frost Protection Triggered." This is normal behavior. It is working.

### Settings

These settings control the safety threshold. Go to **Settings > Safety > Frost Protection**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Frost temperature | 5–12 °C | 7 °C |

**Frost temperature** is the trigger point. If the room temperature hits this number, heating turns on. The minimum is 5 °C. The maximum is 12 °C. The default is 7 °C. Setting it to 5 °C saves the most energy. It allows the house to get quite cold before reacting. Setting it to 12 °C keeps the house comfortably cool in winter. It prevents any risk of dampness from cold surfaces. Most users should stick to 7 °C. It offers a good balance of safety and savings.

### Troubleshooting

*   **The heating turns on all the time.** Check if your room temperature is constantly below the Frost Temperature. If your room is 6 °C and the setting is 7 °C, the heating will run almost constantly to try to get above 7 °C. It might never reach it if heat loss is too high. This looks like a fault, but it is the system trying to meet the target. Improve your insulation. Seal drafts. If the room is cold for other reasons, check for blockages in the heating system.
*   **Pipes froze despite Frost Protection.** Did the power go out? The T2 and receiver need power to work. If the power is out, the boiler does not run. The boiler itself may have its own frost stat. Check your boiler manual. If the temperature sensor was faulty, it might have read a high temperature while the room was actually cold. Check the sensor placement. Is it in a cold draft? Move it. If the sensor is faulty, replace the wall unit.
*   **I want to turn it off for summer.** You cannot. Frost Protection is permanently enabled. This is correct. In summer, the room temperature will rarely drop below 7 °C. Therefore, Frost Protection will never trigger. It will remain dormant. It costs nothing in summer. It does not consume energy when not active. It is always there as a guardian. Do not worry about it in warmer months.
*   **The setting does not save.** Ensure you are not in a restricted mode. Sometimes, if the system is updating firmware, settings are locked. Wait for the update to finish. If you are in the app, ensure you are connected to Wi-Fi. If offline, some settings might not push to the device. Try changing the setting on the wall unit directly.

## 10. Energy Reports

The Hearthline T2 tracks your energy usage. It does not measure gas consumption directly. Instead, it estimates it based on boiler running hours. A boiler running longer usually means more gas used. The system records how many minutes the boiler is active each day. It breaks this down into a graph.

These reports help you see patterns. Are you heating too much in the morning? Are you leaving the heat on during the weekend? You can spot inefficiencies. You can adjust your habits. You can save money. The data is shown in the app. It is also emailed to you. This keeps you informed without opening the app.

### How to

View and manage your energy reports.

1.  **View Weekly Email.** Open your email inbox. Look for the "Hearthline Weekly Report." It arrives every Monday morning. It covers the previous week. It shows a bar chart of daily running hours. It compares your week to the previous week. It highlights any days with unusually high usage.
2.  **View Monthly Summary in App.** Open the Hearthline App. Tap on your device. Tap **Energy** or **Reports**. You will see a dashboard. There is a "Month" view. It shows the total running hours for the month. It shows a trend line. You can tap on individual days to see the exact hours. This view is always available.
3.  **Check Daily Running Hours.** In the app, tap on any day in the history view. It will show the number of hours the boiler ran. For example, "Mon: 4.5 hours." This helps you correlate usage with your activities. Did you have guests? Did you dry clothes inside? These factors increase run time.
4.  **Toggle Weekly Email.** If you do not want emails, go to **Settings > Notifications > Email Reports**. Toggle "Weekly Email" to Off. You can turn it back on anytime. The Monthly Summary in the app cannot be turned off. It is part of the core data logging.

### Settings

Configure how you receive data. Go to **Settings > Notifications**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Weekly email | On/Off | On |
| Monthly summary | Always On | Always On |

**Weekly email** sends a PDF or HTML email to your registered address. The default is On. This is helpful for users who do not check the app daily. It provides a quick overview. If you prefer privacy or less clutter, turn it Off. Note that you will still need to check the app for detailed analysis.

**Monthly summary** is internal to the app. It is **Always On**. You cannot disable data logging. This data is used to improve the app’s insights. It also allows you to track long-term trends. If you sell your home, you can show these reports to potential buyers to demonstrate energy efficiency.

### Troubleshooting

*   **I am not receiving the email.** Check your spam folder. Whitelist the sender "no-reply@hearthline.com". Check your email address in the app settings. Is it correct? Go to **Settings > Account > Email**. Verify it. If correct, tap "Resend Last Report" in the notification settings. Check your Wi-Fi. If the device is offline for a long time, it may miss the upload window for the weekly report.
*   **The running hours seem wrong.** The T2 measures the boiler's "call for heat" time. It does not measure the actual gas flame duration if the boiler modulates. A modern condensing boiler might run at 30% power for a long time. The T2 counts this as "running." This is an approximation. It is consistent over time, which is what matters for trends. Do not expect it to match your gas bill exactly. Gas prices change. Boiler efficiency changes. Use it for relative comparison (this week vs last week).
*   **The graph is empty.** Ensure the device is online. The data must sync to the cloud. Go to **Settings > Sync**. Force a sync. Wait for the green checkmark. Then check the Energy tab. If the device has just been installed, there may be no history yet. Wait 24 hours for data to accumulate.
*   **I want to see hourly data.** The standard reports show daily totals. For deeper analysis, look at the "Activity Log" in the app. It shows start and stop times for the boiler. You can manually add these up for hourly precision. This is advanced. The daily summary is sufficient for most homeowners.

## 11. Child Lock

Child Lock prevents accidental changes. Children are curious. They might spin the ring. They might set the temperature to 30 °C. They might mess with the schedule. Child Lock disables the physical controls on the wall unit. The screen may still display information. Or it may be dimmed. But the ring will not respond to rotation. You cannot change the temperature via the wall unit.

This lock is set via a PIN code. Only those who know the PIN can unlock it. The app can also be locked, but this feature focuses on the physical wall unit. It gives parents peace of mind. It keeps the schedule stable.

### How to

Enable and manage Child Lock.

1.  **Access Child Lock.** Go to **Menu > Settings > Security > Child Lock** on the wall unit. Or **Settings > Security** in the app.
2.  **Turn Lock On.** Tap the "Lock" toggle to "On." A popup will ask you to set a PIN.
3.  **Set Your PIN.** Enter a 4-digit number. Use numbers you can remember. Do not use "1234" or "0000." Confirm the PIN by entering it again. Tap Save.
4.  **Test the Lock.** Try to rotate the ring. Nothing will happen. The screen may show a padlock icon. This confirms the lock is active.
5.  **Unlock the Wall Unit.** To make changes, you must unlock it. Tap the screen or rotate the ring. A PIN entry screen will appear. Enter your 4-digit PIN. If correct, the screen unlocks. You can now adjust the temperature. After a few minutes of inactivity, it will lock again automatically.

### Settings

Secure your device. Go to **Settings > Security > Child Lock**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Lock | On/Off | Off |
| PIN | 4 digits | Set when lock is first turned on |

**Lock** is the main switch. It is **Off** by default. You must turn it On to enable protection. When Off, the ring works normally. When On, the ring is disabled.

**PIN** is a 4-digit numeric code. There is no default PIN for security reasons. You must create one the first time you turn on the lock. Store this PIN in a secure password manager. If you forget the PIN, you may need to factory reset the wall unit. This wipes all data. You would have to set up Wi-Fi and schedules again.

### Troubleshooting

*   **I forgot my PIN.** There is no way to recover the PIN digitally for the wall unit. You must factory reset the device. Remove the batteries. Hold the reset button (usually a small pinhole on the back) for 10 seconds while inserting batteries. The device will wipe itself. You will need to re-pair with the receiver and re-connect to Wi-Fi.
*   **The lock is on, but I want to change the temperature.** Open the Hearthline App. The Child Lock on the *wall unit* does not always lock the *app* if you are the Owner. Check your user role. As Owner, you can change the temperature via the app even if the physical lock is on. This is a feature for parents who want to control the house from their phone but prevent kids from touching the wall. If you want the app locked too, look for "Remote Control Lock" in settings.
*   **The screen does not unlock after entering the PIN.** Ensure you are entering the digits correctly. Watch for the on-screen keyboard. Ensure "Num Lock" is active if visible. Restart the wall unit. Remove batteries. Reinsert. Try again. If the screen is unresponsive to touch, clean it with a dry cloth. Finger oils can sometimes interfere with capacitive screens.
*   **Kids are still changing settings.** Are they changing the temperature on their own phones? You have invited them as users. To stop this, change their role. Go to **Settings > Users**. Change their role from "Member" to "Guest." Guests can view the schedule and temperature. But they **cannot change** the schedule or target temperature. They cannot bypass the Child Lock or the app controls.

## 12. Multi-User Access

Your home is shared. Your partner, children, or flatmates all need control. The Hearthline App allows multiple users. You can invite people. You can give them different levels of control. This is called "Multi-User Access." It keeps the administration simple. You (the Owner) manage the system. Others use it.

There are three roles: Owner, Member, and Guest. Each has different permissions. This ensures that not everyone can delete your schedule. It ensures that guests do not mess up your energy savings.

### How to

Invite users and set their roles.

1.  **Open User Management.** Open the Hearthline App. Tap **Settings > Users & Access**. You will see a list of current users. You are listed as "Owner."
2.  **Invite a User.** Tap "Invite New User." Enter their email address. Select their initial role (Member is usually best). Tap "Send Invite."
3.  **User Accepts Invite.** The invited user will receive an email. They must click the link. This downloads the app if they haven't already. They sign up or log in. The Hearthline T2 will automatically appear in their app.
4.  **Adjust Roles.** You can change a user’s role at any time. Tap on the user in the list. Select "Edit Role." Choose Owner, Member, or Guest. Tap Save. The change is instant.
5.  **Remove a User.** If someone moves out, tap their name. Select "Remove User." They lose access immediately. Their data is deleted from the home group.

### Settings

Manage permissions. Go to **Settings > Users & Access**.

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Users | Up to 8 per home | 1 (Owner) |
| Roles | Owner, Member, Guest | Owner |

**Users** limit is 8. This is the maximum number of people who can control the device via the app. This includes you. You can add 7 others. This is enough for large families or shared houses. If you need more, contact support for enterprise solutions.

**Roles** define what a user can do.
*   **Owner:** Full control. Can invite users, change Wi-Fi, update firmware, see billing info.
*   **Member:** Can change temperature, set manual holds, use Boost, edit the schedule. Cannot invite users or change system settings.
*   **Guest:** Can view the temperature and status. Can use Manual Hold and Boost. **Cannot change the schedule.** Cannot change Eco or Holiday settings. This is ideal for children or occasional visitors.

### Troubleshooting

*   **Invite email is not delivered.** Check for typos in the email address. Check the user’s spam folder. Ensure your email server is not blocking the invite domain. Try sending the invite again. If it fails multiple times, ensure the invited user has installed the Hearthline App and created an account first. Then try adding their existing account by email.
*   **User cannot see the device.** Ensure they are logged into the correct account. Check if they have accepted the invite. Sometimes it takes a few minutes to sync. Have them pull down to refresh the app. Check if their phone is on the same Wi-Fi for the initial handshake. If they are away, ensure they have Wi-Fi or mobile data.
*   **Member cannot change the schedule.** Check their role. If they are a Guest, they cannot change the schedule. Change them to Member. If they are a Member but still cannot edit, check if the Weekly Schedule is locked by the Owner. Go to **Settings > Schedule > Lock**. Ensure the schedule edit permission is not disabled for all users. Also, check if a Holiday Mode or Away Mode is active. Some users might perceive a "grayed out" schedule as a lock, but it is actually because the system is in a priority mode. Try canceling the holiday or leaving the geofence to test schedule editing.
*   **I accidentally removed myself as Owner.** If you are the only user and you remove yourself, the device may be orphaned. Contact Hearthline Support immediately. They can help reset the administrative access. To prevent this, always have a second trusted user with Owner rights, or be very careful when managing user lists. Do not remove the last Owner account.

## Error Codes

Sometimes things go wrong. The Hearthline T2 will tell you what is wrong. It shows an error code on the screen. It also appears in the app. This table explains the five possible codes. It tells you what they mean and what you shoulddo. Do not panic. Most errors are easy to fix.

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **E1** | No Wi-Fi connection | Check that your router is on. Ensure the wall unit is within range of the router. Restart your router. Go to **Menu > Network > Wi-Fi Setup** and reconnect. |
| **E2** | Temperature sensor fault | The internal sensor may be broken or disconnected. Try restarting the wall unit by removing the batteries for 30 seconds. If the error persists, contact support for a replacement sensor. |
| **E3** | Receiver not responding | The wall unit cannot talk to the receiver box. Check if the receiver has power. Move the wall unit closer to the receiver to test the radio signal. Press the pairing button on the receiver to re-pair the devices. |
| **E4** | Wall unit battery low | The batteries are running out. Replace both AA batteries with fresh alkaline batteries immediately. Do not mix old and new batteries. The screen may dim before this code appears. |
| **E5** | Firmware update failed | The software update did not complete. Do not turn off the power. Try to restart the wall unit. The system will attempt to resume the update. If it loops, use the app to force a re-download or contact support. |

## Specifications

These are the technical details of your Hearthline T2. Use this table for reference when buying parts or checking compatibility.

| Feature | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Display** | 3.5-inch touch screen with rotating ring |
| **Power (Wall Unit)** | 2 AA batteries (approx. 2 years life) OR 24 V AC wiring |
| **Power (Receiver Box)** | Mains powered (installed by qualified installer) |
| **Wi-Fi Connectivity** | 2.4 GHz only |
| **Radio Range** | Up to 30 m indoors (between wall unit and receiver) |
| **Temperature Control Range** | 5–30 °C in 0.5 °C steps |
| **Eco Temperature Range** | 10–20 °C |
| **Holiday Temperature Range** | 5–15 °C |
| **Frost Protection Range** | 5–12 °C |
| **Geofence Radius** | 200–2,000 m |
| **Boost Duration Options** | 30, 60, 90, 120 minutes |
| **Hot Water Boost Options** | 30, 60 minutes |
| **Max Users** | 8 per home |
| **Child Lock PIN** | 4 digits |
| **Operating System Support** | iOS and Android via Hearthline App |

# Hearthline T2 Smart Thermostat User Manual

Welcome to the Hearthline T2. This manual is designed to help you understand, set up, and get the most out of your new smart thermostat. The Hearthline T2 is built for homes with gas or oil boilers. It replaces your old wall dial or programmer. It gives you precise control over your home’s heating. It helps you save energy. It keeps your home comfortable.

**This manual describes Firmware 2.0.** To check your current firmware version, go to **Menu > Settings > About**. If your version is older, please update via the app to ensure all features described here work correctly.

This guide covers everything from the very first day of use to advanced settings. We have written this manual for homeowners, not engineers. The language is simple. The steps are clear. We explain technical terms when they first appear. If you need to find a specific setting, look for the bold menu path, such as **Menu > Heating > Schedule**. This tells you exactly where to go on the screen or in the app.

Please read the Safety Information first. Then, proceed through the chapters in order. Each chapter covers one main feature. By the end of this manual, you will feel confident using your Hearthline T2. You will be able to adjust settings with ease. You will understand how the system works. Let us begin.

## Safety Information

Your safety and the safety of others are our top priority. The Hearthline T2 is a safe device when used correctly. However, it involves electricity and heat. Please read these important warnings before you start using your thermostat. Keep this manual in a safe place. You may need it in the future. If you give this device to someone else, give them this manual too.

*   **Qualified Installation Only for the Receiver Box.** The receiver box connects directly to your boiler. It controls the power to the boiler. This involves mains electricity and potentially hazardous components. **The receiver box must only be opened or installed by a qualified installer.** Do not try to open the receiver box yourself. You could be seriously injured or damage your boiler. The wall unit, however, is designed for you to install. It uses batteries or low-voltage wiring. You can install the wall unit yourself. But the receiver must be handled by a professional.

*   **Avoid Direct Sunlight and Radiators.** The temperature sensor inside the wall unit measures the air temperature in your room. For accurate readings, the sensor must "see" the general room temperature. **Do not install the wall unit in direct sunlight.** The sun will heat the plastic casing. The sensor will read a false high temperature. Your heating will stay off when it should be on. **Do not install the wall unit above a radiator.** Heat rises. A radiator heats the air directly above it. If the thermostat is near a heat source, it will read a false high temperature. Install the wall unit on an internal wall. Choose a spot away from windows, doors, and heat sources. Ideally, place it at eye level. This is about 1.5 meters from the floor. This position gives the most accurate reading of the living space temperature.

*   **Keep Small Parts Away from Children.** The Hearthline T2 comes with small screws and wall plugs. These are small enough to be swallowed. They can cause choking hazards. **Keep all small parts away from children and pets.** When you install the wall unit, check the floor afterward. Pick up any dropped screws or plugs immediately. Dispose of packaging materials properly. Plastic bags and foam can also be dangerous for babies and toddlers. Store the extra parts in a high, locked cupboard if you have young children.

*   **Battery Safety.** The wall unit can run on two AA batteries. **Use only high-quality alkaline batteries.** Do not mix old and new batteries. Do not mix different brands of batteries. Do not use rechargeable batteries unless they are specifically rated for low-drift devices, as some rechargeables have lower voltage profiles that may cause reading errors. If you use the battery option, insert the batteries correctly. Match the plus (+) and minus (-) signs in the battery compartment. Incorrect insertion can damage the device. If the battery compartment is damaged or leaking fluid, stop using the wall unit immediately. Clean the contacts with a dry cloth. If corrosion is present, do not touch the fluid. The fluid is corrosive. It can burn your skin. Wear gloves. Dispose of the wall unit according to local electronic waste regulations. Do not throw batteries in the regular trash. Recycle them at a designated drop-off point.

*   **Wi-Fi Connectivity and Health.** The Hearthline T2 uses Wi-Fi to connect to your home network. Wi-Fi uses radio waves. These are non-ionizing radiation. They are generally considered safe for home use. However, if you have concerns about electromagnetic fields (EMF), you can minimize exposure. You can position the wall unit away from beds or prolonged seating areas. You can also disconnect the Wi-Fi in the app settings if you only want local control. Note that without Wi-Fi, you cannot use remote control features or receive weather updates. The device will still work as a local timer. The radio connection between the wall unit and the receiver is very low power. It is designed to be safe. It complies with all relevant safety standards. If you have a pacemaker or other implanted electronic device, consult your doctor. Some devices are sensitive to strong magnetic fields, though the T2’s fields are very weak.

*   **Water and Moisture.** The wall unit is designed for indoor use in dry rooms. **Do not install the wall unit in a bathroom, shower room, or any area with high humidity or water spray.** Water can short-circuit the electronics. It can cause the screen to malfunction. It can create a shock hazard. Do not clean the unit with a wet cloth. Use a slightly damp cloth only if necessary, and dry it immediately. Never submerge the wall unit in water. Do not splash water on it. If water does get inside, remove the batteries immediately. Let it dry completely for 48 hours before testing. If it does not work after drying, contact support. Do not attempt to repair it yourself.

*   **Choking Hazard for Batteries.** If the wall unit uses 24 V AC wiring, it may not have a battery compartment accessible from the front. If it does, and you have young children, be aware that button cells and AA batteries can be swallowed. Swallowing a battery is a medical emergency. It can cause severe internal burns within hours. If you suspect a child has swallowed a battery, seek emergency medical help immediately. Keep spare batteries in a container that cannot be opened by children.

## 1. Getting Started

Congratulations on your new Hearthline T2. This chapter explains how to get your system working. You will pair the wall unit with the receiver. You will connect the device to your home Wi-Fi. You will create an account in the Hearthline app. This setup takes about fifteen minutes. You will need your home Wi-Fi password. You will need your smartphone. You do not need tools for this part. The physical installation of the receiver is done by your installer. The physical installation of the wall unit is covered in a separate quick-start card. Here, we focus on the software setup.

### How to

Follow these steps to complete the initial setup. Make sure the receiver box is powered on and has been configured by your installer. Make sure the wall unit has batteries inserted or is wired for power. The screen on the wall unit should turn on.

1.  **Wake the Wall Unit.** Tap the center of the screen or rotate the ring slightly. The screen will light up. You will see a welcome message. It may ask you to select a language.
2.  **Pair the Wall Unit.** On the screen, look for the message "Pairing..." or go to **Menu > Settings > Pairing**. If the wall unit is new, it will automatically try to find the receiver.
